entries.body:
Ticket: TALA-92 — Bug: KB sidebar tree forgets collapse state — every visit re-expands all folders; want collapsed default + collapsible space sections

TALA-92 — KB sidebar tree expansion state: persisted, collapsed by default, space sections collapsible.

Root cause: every KbDocRow held `expanded = $state(true)` component-local, so navigating away unmounted the tree and every remount re-expanded everything; a fresh view opened fully expanded for the same reason, and space sections had no collapse control at all.

What changed (3 commits on agent/tala-92-bug-kb-sidebar-tree-forgets-collapse-sta, base rc):
- New ui/src/lib/knowledge-tree-state.svelte.ts: one $state-backed singleton for the whole tree, persisted through the house view-memory pattern (session-scoped per tab, sessionStorage, tolerant parse — garbage/non-boolean shapes degrade to defaults). Absent key = collapsed, so the collapsed default and the safe parse are one rule. API: docExpanded/toggleDoc, sectionExpanded/toggleSection, openPath (opens a chain + section, never closes anything), resetKbTreeState for tests.
- KbDocRow: `expanded` is now `$derived(kbTreeState.docExpanded(doc.id))`; the chevron writes through the store. Nested-doc create opens the parent through the store, not row state. KbDocTree's drop-inside opens the target folder so a moved doc is visible where it lands.
- KbSpaceRow: each space section gets a real chevron (design option a); clicking the space NAME still selects and now also opens its section — only-opens, the chevron alone collapses.
- Knowledge.svelte: the section gate is the store's AND the active space's (the doc list is keyed to the active space, so a non-active open section must not render someone else's docs). An ancestor-chain effect opens the selected/restored doc's chain on arrival — restore, permalinks, nested create — guarded by a latch so the effect and the user don't fight: each (space, doc) pair is opened once, after which a manual collapse stands. A one-line note: the latch deliberately deviates from the plan's compound-skip sketch, which would have re-opened manually collapsed branches; reasoning in the code comment.
- changelog/2026-11-04-kb-sidebar-tree-expansion.md per the unreleased-entry convention.

Verification: bun run gate green end to end — check (invariants, docs 1019 links, gen-docs, changelog, judge-pr, pr-watch, cleanup-sweep), svelte-check 0 errors / 0 warnings, ui vitest 201 files / 3069 tests all passing including the 9 new store tests (round-trip, garbage parse, non-boolean shapes, private mode, openPath never-closes, no-op writes). Diff reviewed by hand before push; push passed the repo's pre-push gate. KNOWN LIMITATION: no live browser pass on this box — no Docker, no postgres binaries, so the dev stack could not boot here; the flow was verified by the gates above and rc's ui CI plus a manual look at the Knowledge sidebar is the remaining confirmation.

Reviewer, look hardest at: the ancestor-chain latch in Knowledge.svelte (the effect-vs-user interplay is the one subtle piece), the section gate's active-space coupling, and that view-memory's once-per-tab read latch is respected (the store hydrates lazily on first use, not at module load).

## Plan

Fix KB sidebar tree expansion-state persistence in ui/src/routes/app (repo outcrop-labs/talaria). Mechanism confirmed by code read: KbDocRow.svelte holds `let expanded = $state(true)` component-local, so remount resets it; no persistence. Approach: (1) new lib module knowledge-tree-state.ts (or extend knowledge-selection.ts) following the view-memory.ts house pattern - session-scoped, per-tab, sessionStorage-backed, written only while on the view, restored once on arrival, storing { [docId]: boolean } expansion map plus per-space section booleans, tolerant parse (garbage -> defaults); (2) KbDocRow initializes expanded from the store and writes through on toggle, default collapsed (false) when no stored state; (3) Knowledge.svelte/KbSpaceRow.svelte: space sections get a chevron + collapsible state (design option a - each space row has its own chevron, several sections may sit open, selecting a space still drives the main pane; tree under a space renders when its section is open); active doc's space section force-opens on arrival so view-memory restore remains visible; (4) preserve nested-doc creation auto-expanding the parent chain and space section; (5) verify drag-and-drop reparenting still works with collapsed parents; (6) add regression tests in the style of view-memory.test.ts for store read/write/parse-garbage. Files touched: ui/src/routes/app/KbDocRow.svelte, KbSpaceRow.svelte, Knowledge.svelte, new ui/src/lib/knowledge-tree-state.ts, test file beside it. Testing: bun run check + ui vitest for the new store tests + svelte-check, then browser verification against the dev server (collapse, navigate away and back, fresh view collapsed, sections collapsible, nested-create auto-expand, DnD).🔧 Opened by **Doug** (`doug-engineering`) via the Talaria workbench (standard effort). Commits on this branch are authored by the agent.

entries.title: cost: unpriced cloud usage prices itself where a price exists — admins fix the rest
entries.body:
## Why every instance showed "Unpriced cloud usage"

The dollars on a usage row are computed when it is read, by the priced view in `talaria-gateway/src/usage.rs`. The view is the same on `main` 805e6799 and `rc` f198720c. It takes the provider's own charge first, and otherwise a published price from `provider_prices`. It did not read admin-entered rates. Four things combined:

1. **On `main`, every agent turn on an OpenRouter endpoint is unpriced, permanently.** `record_usage` is the per-turn writer that chat, channel replies and the harness use. It writes no provider charge, no serving variant and no generation id. The view refused OpenRouter's model-level price for any row without a variant, so these rows could never be priced. A model served by a pool of endpoints gets `endpoint = NULL` and can never be priced either. On `rc` the relay books every call with OpenRouter's `usage.cost`, which OpenRouter now always sends, so new rows are priced. The 30 days of history from `main` would have kept the alert firing after the upgrade.
2. **Admins had no way to fix it.** Since ef2948a9 the editable rates are not read, and the endpoint editor's pricing section is read-only. The alert's advice, "Set prices on /models", pointed at something nobody could do.
3. **The catalog matcher misses real provider ids.** Run against the live OpenRouter catalog, these fail: OpenAI's `-YYYY-MM-DD` snapshots (`gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`), xAI's `-MMDD` ids (`grok-4-0709`), and Fireworks-style path ids.
4. **Plan-priced endpoints are mispriced and cannot be marked "included".** On a Z.ai Coding Plan key, `/models` publishes no prices and the completion `usage` has no cost. All 12 of its GLM ids match OpenRouter's pay-as-you-go entries, so plan usage was priced as if billed per token. This was observed with the real key.

None of these failures recorded a reason anywhere. If the catalog fetch failed, nothing said so.

The evidence (the matcher run against the live catalog, the SQL reproduction against each writer's row shape, and the live test logs) is in the session's `release/unpriced/` directory.

## What changed

- **The price decision, applied in order.** Each step is labelled in `cost_basis`, and the order is pinned by `price_basis` and a live parity test:
  1. the provider's charge (`provider`);
  2. an admin's **included in a plan** ($0, `included`), ahead of any published price;
  3. a **published price** (`derived`): the serving variant's when the call names one, otherwise the model-level price for every provider, OpenRouter included;
  4. an admin's **manual rate** (`manual`), the fallback.

  Cache tokens are billed at the catalog's own `input_cache_write` / `input_cache_read` rates when it publishes them. The 1.25× / 0.1× multipliers apply only when it does not.
- **Pricing is computed at read time.** A saved decision, or a price found later, re-prices every past row of that model. That clears the alert for history, not only for new usage.
- **Oracle.**
  - It records each (endpoint, model) outcome in `price_lookups`: `priced`, `no_match` (with the ids it tried), or `source_failed` (quoting the source's own error).
  - It stores cache rates.
  - It matches the `-YYYY-MM-DD` and validated `-MMDD` snapshot shapes, and takes the last segment of a multi-segment id.
  - `lookup_now` does a targeted lookup and waits for it.
- **API (admin only).**
  - `GET /api/cost/unpriced` lists unpriced models with their reasons, plus the settings admins have made.
  - `PUT` / `DELETE /api/cost/prices` set or remove a setting. Both are audited, and the answer includes `repriced`.
  - `POST /api/cost/unpriced/lookup` runs a lookup on demand.

  `docs/api/**` is regenerated.
- **UI.**
  - Observability → Cost now has an admin-only **Unpriced models** panel. Each row shows the endpoint, model, tokens and reason, with **Set price** (input, output, cache write, cache read per 1M), **Included in a plan**, and **Retry lookup**.
  - A **Priced by an admin** list shows each setting, what it currently prices, and when a published price has taken over. Each setting can be removed.
  - The endpoint editor shows these settings and adds an **Included in a plan** checklist.
  - The per-model legend and the spend tile label included tokens instead of showing $0.
- **The alert** is now shown to admins only. It links to `/observability/cost#unpriced` and says what to do.
- **Migrations.** These are appended at the end of the migration list, and the schema snapshot is regenerated:
  - `provider_prices` gets cache rate columns;
  - new table `model_price_overrides`, keyed by the ledger's own endpoint text, so history under a deleted endpoint (or no endpoint) can still be priced;
  - new table `price_lookups`.

## Verified

- Unit tests, `cargo test -p talaria-price-oracle -p talaria-gateway -p talaria-alerts -p talaria-routes-comms --lib`:
  - id matching against ids from the live catalog;
  - the date-strip shapes;
  - the cache rates parsed from the observed `/endpoints` payload;
  - `price_basis` precedence;
  - each reason branch;
  - body and semantic validation;
  - the alert text and its link.
- `#[ignore]` live tests against a migrated Postgres. Rows are booked through `record_relay_usage`, or inserted in `main`'s `record_usage` shape. The tests check that:
  - a manual price re-prices history, and a published price later takes over (the setting is then marked shadowed);
  - included is $0 with its label, and wins over a published price but not over the provider's charge;
  - OpenRouter rows without a variant (`main`'s per-turn row, and `rc`'s cut-off stream) are priced, and an exact variant wins over the model-level price;
  - the SQL and `price_basis` agree on nine cases;
  - a failed source is quoted as the reason;
  - the unpriced alert clears for history once a price lands.
- ui tests for the panel helpers and the spend legend; `svelte-check` is clean.
- Exercised in the running app on a worktree stack (headless Chromium, so nothing reached a real desktop or browser):
  - **Calls.** Three real gateway calls went to a Z.ai Coding Plan endpoint, using the real key sealed by the api. The ledger also got OpenRouter rows (shaped as `main`'s per-turn row), OpenAI dated-id and Groq relay rows, a row on a deleted endpoint, and a no-endpoint row, each in its writer's own columns.
  - **Catalog unreachable.** OpenRouter was blocked by a proxy, with the Z.ai calls exempted. The panel listed all 7 models with their reasons ("source didn't answer", quoting the full cause chain; "endpoint removed"; "no endpoint recorded"). The alert linked straight to the panel. Retry still failed and said so. **Included in a plan** on `glm-4.6` priced it at $0 and labelled it in the panel and the legend. **Set price** on the deleted endpoint's model re-priced its history. An empty rate showed the form's error.
  - **Catalog reachable.** Retry found a price for `glm-4.5-air`, for the `main`-shape OpenRouter history ($0.21 across 2 calls, derived from OpenRouter's own model price with its published cache-read rate), and for `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` (the new date strip). Groq's `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` came back "no published price found", naming the catalog and what was tried, and was then priced by hand.
  - **Endpoint editor.** Its plan checklist marked the pay-as-you-go-priced `glm-4.5-air` as included.
  - **Result.** `unpricedCloudTokens` went from 154,572 to 0, the month spend from $0 to $0.27, and 142 tokens were labelled "included in a plan". The alert was gone. A removed setting re-priced back to the published price, a second removal answered 404, and a contradictory body answered 400 with its sentence. A member gets 403 on all four routes and never sees the alert. Every write landed in the audit log.
- `bun run gate`. The first run hit a 10s `afterAll` timeout in `ui/src/sdk/client-docs.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch. It is an `rmSync` on this host's stalling disk; the file passes on its own, and the re-run gate passed.

## Not verified

- Live calls with an OpenRouter, OpenAI or Groq key; none was available. Those rows were booked in the writers' column shapes, not by real calls.
- A client instance's own data. There was no access, by design.
- Whether client fleets actually run on OpenRouter. Cause 1 assumes they do; causes 2 to 4 apply whatever provider is used.
- The `api/tests/it/price_rig_live.rs` edit, which now reads the real view instead of a copy, is compiled and run in CI only.

entries.title: tasks: a ticket moves between boards — for people and for agents (move_ticket)
entries.body:
Tickets move between boards — for people from the ticket detail and the card/row menu, and for agents through a new toolkit tool, `move_ticket`. For v0.13.0.

## The design

1. **Permissions.** A person needs editor or owner on the source board and on the destination. A board they cannot see answers 403, whether it exists or not (the boards family's "forbidden, not hidden" rule). An agent needs board policy (`board_allows_agent`) on both boards. On the source it asks `agent_ticket_refusal`, the predicate every agent ticket write asks, so a ticket that is closed, archived or on an archived board refuses with the same sentence. The toolkit has no approval queue for ticket writes (`triage_ticket` is not gated either), so `move_ticket` follows that class: no approval queue, and the server enforces the rules.
2. **Status.** The caller may name a column on the destination. Otherwise the server maps by name (key or label), then by category, then to the destination's intake. **A move never closes a ticket.** An open ticket never lands in a done or off-board column, and a person naming one gets a 400. An agent is refused any closed column (403). An agent also keeps its HITL stops: no moving a ticket in review, blocked, or stranded, and no entering an agent-start (pickup) column it was not already in, because entering one is assignment. A ticket a person already closed stays closed (done → the destination's done column).
3. **Labels** map by name (exact, then ignoring case, using the destination's spelling). Labels the destination does not have are **dropped, never created**. They are named in `moved.labelsDropped` and on the activity line.
4. **Assignees.** **Unassign and note.** A person who cannot see the destination, or an agent it does not allow, is removed and named in `moved.unassigned` and the activity line. If they stayed assigned, the assignment would say they own work they cannot open, and dispatch would refuse the agent anyway.
5. **Keys.** The ticket takes the destination's next number (`boards.ticket_seq`, in the same transaction). Its old (board, number) goes into a new `task_ref_aliases` table. `resolve_task_id` falls back to that table when no live ticket holds a ref, so `PLAT-118` still opens the ticket. Old `/boards/<old>/<ticket>` links follow it: the ticket id never changes, and the ticket view redirects to the board the ticket is on now.
6. **Linked state.** Comments and the room, activity, reviews, judge verdicts, usage, attachments and dependencies are keyed by ticket id, so they come along. Dependencies may already cross boards. The room's topic is re-written with the new ref, and the ticket and every comment are re-indexed under the new board: `payload.boardId` is the retrieval ACL, so without this the old board's members would keep finding them. Watchers who cannot see the destination stay stored but **dormant**, which is the existing rule for a person removed from a board; they are named in `moved.dormantWatchers`. A sub-task **leaves its parent** behind, because sub-tasks live on their parent's board. Three things refuse with 409 instead of half-moving: a **live work session**, a **workchain step** (chains are board-scoped and readiness reads one board's columns), and a ticket **with sub-tasks**. A reviewer's sign-off (`approved_at`) does not travel unless the ticket is closed.
7. **Events.** `publish_board` goes to both boards, so both views update live. The activity row reads "moved from A (A-5) to B (B-1) · labels dropped … · unassigned …", plus a `status` row when the column key changed (the approvals inbox reads that row). The audit row is `task.board_move`, with before and after board, ref and status. Notifications go to the destination audience: watchers, assigned people and the creator who can see the new board, never the mover (`ticket_audience`, the same set a status move tells). Anyone who cannot see the new board is not told where it went. A ticket leaving review resolves the old board's sign-off rows.
8. **API.** `POST /api/tasks/{id}/move { boardId, status?, preview? }`. It is an action, so POST. `status` is the destination's column **key**, the same field `PUT /api/tasks/{id}` takes, not a `statusId`: default columns have no row id. `preview: true` returns the same `moved` summary and writes nothing. The confirm dialog reads it, the same pattern as the board team move's `previewAccessLoss`. It answers 200 `{ task, moved }` or `{ preview: true, moved }`, otherwise 400, 403, 404 or 409. `docs/api/**` is regenerated.
9. **UI.** **Move to board…** appears in the ticket detail's footer and in the card and row menu (editors only). The dialog uses the `Modal`, `Select` and `Button` primitives. It offers only the boards the person can add tickets to, and the destination's columns, never a done one for an open ticket. Before the Move button it shows the server's own preview: the ref change (and that the old ref still opens it), the column, dropped labels, unassigned people, a parent left behind, a sign-off cleared, and watchers going quiet. There is no multi-board view, so there is no drag between boards.
10. **Agent tool.** `move_ticket(taskId, boardId, status?, preview?)`. It uses `taskId` and the board's status **key**, the same names `triage_ticket` and every other ticket tool use, rather than `ticketId` or `statusId`. The description states the refusals with the shared `OFF_THE_TABLE` and `COMMENT_INSTEAD` constants, so the prose gate holds it. It is wired into the fitness catalog (`talaria-fitness-talaria-tools`), the sandbox (a backend with production's refusals, plus a test), `BACKED_TOOLS`, the chips test (a move answers one link, the ticket on its new board), `ui/src/lib/chips.ts` `TOOL_FIELDS`, `mcp/README.md` (the tools table and the enforcement table), and the `talaria-toolkit` skill. `hermes_authority.rs` is a fitness harness about Notion-versus-Talaria, not a list of tool classes, so it was left alone.

## Verified

- `bun run gate`: check, the ui typecheck and tests, the mcp typecheck, and fmt, clippy and tests for talaria-api, -api-routes, -chips, -fitness-talaria-tools, -fitness-toolbox, -routes-boards, -statuses and -tasks.
- `cargo test -p talaria-tasks moving`: the status, label and summary mappings, for a person and for an agent.
- `bun run test -- ticket-move`: the dialog's destination filter and its "what changes" lines.
- `cargo test -p talaria-api --test it task_move_live:: -- --ignored`: 4 live-DB tests passed.
  - The permission matrix: not on the destination, viewer of the destination, viewer of the source, unknown board, same board, no session.
  - An agent is refused a board it is not on, `done`, `cancelled`, and a ticket in review.
  - Re-key, and the old ref resolving, through the real router.
  - Labels are dropped and not created, and the person not on the destination is unassigned.
  - The activity line and the audit row are written.
  - A preview writes nothing.
  - A live work session refuses with 409, and the move succeeds once the session ends.
- The schema replay and snapshot (`migrations:check --update-snapshot` on an empty database): the only change is `task_ref_aliases`.
- In the running app, on a worktree stack with two boards that have different columns and labels:
  - **A person in a real browser (headless Chromium).** The card menu offers Move to board…. The dialog previewed PLAT-1 → SUP-2, In Progress by name, `urgent` dropped, Bo unassigned and his watch going quiet, and listed no Shipped column. After Move, the ticket is SUP-2 on Support Desk with `Billing` kept. A second tab on each board updated without a reload (the source lost the card and the destination gained it). The old `/boards/<Platform>/<ticket>` URL redirected to Support Desk. The Activity tab shows the move line.
  - **An agent with its own key, through the real toolkit (`mcp/dist` over stdio).** `tools/list` lists `move_ticket`. Preview, then the move PLAT-2 → SUP-1, succeeded. It was refused (403) for a board it is not on, and for `shipped` and `cancelled`. `GET /api/tasks/PLAT-2` returns SUP-1, for the person and for the agent.
  - A person got 400 naming a done column for an open ticket and 400 for a key the board lacks. A sub-task parent and a live work session each got 409. A sub-task moved and left its parent. Only the destination's creator was notified (not the mover, and not the watcher who cannot see it), and that stack has no push or mail configured.

## Not verified

- CI's full api, ui and e2e jobs: they run on this PR.
- The CI live-integration workflow does not run `#[ignore]`d tests on PRs. They ran locally against the worktree database.
- Moving a ticket in review into the destination's review column, and the re-filing of approval rows on the new board: the old board's rows are resolved, but I did not check an approvals inbox on the destination.
- The comment re-index against a live Qdrant (the worktree stack shares the dev sidecars). The ticket and comment docs carry the new `boardId` by construction, and the re-index is fire-and-forget like every other indexing site.
- A queued `work_wait` entry does not hold a move. Dispatch re-checks board policy on the ticket's current board when the slot frees.
- The `move_ticket` fitness probe only has the sandbox backend and a sandbox test. No harness dry-run surface offers it yet.

entries.title: fleet: agent designs are server-owned runs in redis — a reload no longer loses one
entries.body:
#699 is merged into rc, so this diff is this branch's own commits.

The owner's rule: *"No runs should be controlled by the browser state, the state should be in redis and held so that it survives refreshes and etc. Creating agents is one of the most important parts of the platform, so this needs to be durable."*

## What changed

**Where state lives.** Redis holds one record per person: the hash `agent-design:<user>`, fields `rev` and `json`, with a 72 h TTL refreshed on every write.
- The record has the status (generating, ready or error), the instruction and purpose, the chat, the validated draft, the draft a refine started from, the error, and the started, finished and updated timestamps.
- Every write is a compare-and-set on `rev` in one Lua script (`store.rs`), so the api processes never interleave. Nothing about a design is held in process memory.
- The transitions are pure functions in `record.rs`. A run writes only the record whose `runId` is its own, so a discard or a new describe drops a late answer.

**How the run executes.** It is a new `agent-design` kind on the runs runtime, next to `plan-draft` (new crate `talaria-agent-design`, armed in `talaria-jobs`' census).
- POST writes the record, then enqueues the run and returns at once. Nothing waits on the HTTP request, so Cloudflare's 100 s limit is not a factor.
- The step makes the same muse `agent` harness call as `/api/muse`, with the same model chain, member allowlist, ledger caller and error sentences, which are now shared. It then lands the answer in the record.
- A driver that dies is reclaimed by the sweep. If a record says generating but its run has ended, or has had no run row for 60 s, the next read reports it as "stopped before it finished".
- When a design lands and no modal is watching, a bell row is filed (kind `agent-design`, class Work finished, entity `agent_design`, one row per design that a refine re-alerts). The open modal's reads (`?watching=1`) and the start itself set a 12 s watch mark, which suppresses the row. Hiring, discarding or replacing the design marks the row read.

**API: `/api/fleet/agent-design`**, all under `agents.manage` (the hire's permission). `docs/api` is regenerated.
- `GET` → `{ design, now }`. `now` is the server clock, used for the elapsed count.
- `POST { instruction }` starts a design. If one is already generating, it returns that one; an idle design is replaced. `POST { instruction, refine: true, current? }` refines, and answers 409 while one is generating.
- `PATCH { name, handle, department, role, soul, skills }` saves the person's own draft, from review edits, a role template or a manual start. It answers 409 while a run is writing.
- `DELETE { id? }` discards the design and cancels a running run. It answers 404 if there is nothing to discard.
- `POST /api/fleet/create` takes an optional `designId` and consumes that design once the hire is queued.

**UI.**
- `lib/agent-design.svelte.ts` (the module-state orchestration) is deleted. `lib/agent-design.ts` replaces it with the read, the four verbs and pure helpers.
- The modal keeps only view state: the step, the form being typed (saved after a 600 ms pause), and a 1 s clock while a run is going.
- A `run` event on the person's stream refetches the design, and a poll (2 s while watched, 5 s otherwise) covers the gaps.
- **+** shows a dot while a design is generating (accent, pulsing), ready (accent) or failed (danger), and the roster row stays.
- `/agents?design=open` opens the modal. That is where the bell's link points.
- There is a **Discard design** action on both steps.

## Verified
I ran these in headless Chromium against this branch's stack (app :5304, api :5404, fresh DB), with a stand-in OpenAI-compatible model held 3–20 s.
- **Reload during generation:** I reloaded 6.6 s in. The dot on **+** said generating, and the row read "Designing A research analyst…". Reopening the modal resumed the splash with the same purpose, and review came up at 21.0 s.
- **Reload during a refine:** the modal came back on review showing the refined name and the receipt "Refine applied Soul · 1 added · 1 removed lines".
- **Modal closed, tab on Inbox:** one bell row appeared, unread, "Agent design ready: Scout" → `/agents?design=open`. Clicking it opened review. A renamed field was on the server 1.2 s later. **Create agent** queued the hire `sorter`; GET then returned `design: null` and the bell row was read.
- **Second tab:** it showed the same generating design, and both tabs reached review.
- **Discard, then start over:** the server returned null and the describe step was empty. The new describe landed.
- `cargo test -p talaria-agent-design --lib -- --include-ignored`, against the stack's Postgres and Redis:
  - 15 state-machine units.
  - 6 live tests: finish with no client, then read from a fresh session (run `done`, one bell row, TTL > 24 h); a second start follows the first, and a later describe replaces it and reads the old bell row; edit, refine and discard, with edits refused mid-refine; discard mid-run cancels it and drops the answer; a watched landing rings no bell, and a failure lands its sentence; a record whose run is gone reads as stalled.
- 14 ui tests (`lib/agent-design.test.ts`): resume after a reload (opening step; elapsed on the server's clock across two tabs with skewed clocks), the poll, reseed-on-landing-not-on-save, and each verb's request and cache write.
- `bun run gate`: check, svelte-check, vitest (3060), and fmt, clippy and tests for `talaria-agent-design`, `-api-routes`, `-jobs`, `-notify` and `-routes-fleet`.

## Review followups (review-700: SHIP-WITH-FOLLOWUPS — all seven shoulds taken)
- **S1 (ABA in the compare-and-set).** The revision is now a fresh UUID on every write. Before, a counter restarted at 1 after a delete, so a late landing could write a discarded design back over a new one. *Live test:* a swap that names the revision from before the discard fails, and the newer design stays.
- **S2 (hang on a failed first read).** A failed first read now shows "Could not check for a design in progress: …" with **Retry**. Describe and **Configure manually** stay usable.
- **S3 (edits dropped on close).** A pending save is now *flushed*, never dropped: when the modal closes, before **Create**, and on `pagehide` (with `keepalive`). **Configure manually** saves nothing until a name or handle is set (N9). *Headless:* I edited the name, clicked Cancel within 600 ms, and the server had the edit.
- **S4 (false error after Refine).** **Refine** now cancels the pending save, because the edits already travel in its `current`. A save that fires while a run is going is dropped, so the false "not saved" message is gone.
- **S5 (stale tab writes over a newer design).** PATCH and refine now name the design they edit (`id`). A stale tab gets a 409 and is shown the current design; a nameless save is allowed only when no design exists. *Live test:* tab A's save and refine for discarded design X are refused, and manual design Z stays untouched.
- **S6 (Duplicate overwrites the waiting design).** **Duplicate** now has its own empty form. It never reads, saves or spends the waiting design. *Headless:* the form opened empty, and the waiting "Flushed" design was the same design after editing and cancelling.
- **S7 (the design gates the hire).** `/api/fleet/create` with `designId` now claims the design before it enqueues. A second hire from the same design gets a 409. While the hire runs, the design is hidden from the modal, the row and the dot, and edits and refines are refused. A finished hire consumes the design. A failed hire, or one that never appears within 60 s, hands it back on the review step with the hire's sentence. An enqueue that fails hands it back at once. *Live test:* covers all of these paths. *Headless:* the hire claimed the design and the run reached `done`.
- **Nits taken:**
  - N1: a hand edit ends the "Refine applied" receipt.
  - N2: run events refetch only for the design's own run or hire, or when no design is cached.
  - N3: the **+** dot is `StatusDot`.
  - N4: the changelog says "none for the last 12 seconds".
  - N5: a describe over a design whose run is dead starts fresh.
  - N6: the wire carries `chatLength`, not the chat.
  - N7 and N8: Redis RDB durability and the five-minute crash pickup are in the changelog and user doc.
  - N8 itself is not shortened: the lease TTL is the step budget, and cutting it would abandon real 2m20s designs.

**Re-verified:** `cargo test -p talaria-agent-design --lib -- --include-ignored` passes 28 tests (19 unit, 9 live). The ui tests (`lib/agent-design.test.ts`) cover named saves, keepalive, the 409, and pending vs hired. `bun run gate` passed. In headless Chromium I re-ran the core flows on the restarted stack: reload mid-design and mid-refine, a closed modal through the bell to review and a hire, two tabs, and discard then start over. All behaved as before, though the host disk was stalling (IO pressure 30–90%), so landings took longer than the model's hold.

## Fix verification followups (NS1–NS4)

- **NS1 (superseded by NS5 below).** New agent used to wait while a hire held the design. A describe or a manual save in that window would have to replace the design the hire may hand back. Both now answer 409 `Hiring`, and the modal says "Hiring <name> — New agent opens again when this hire finishes". When the hire fails, an open modal moves to review with the hire's reason. When it finishes, an empty describe opens. Duplicate is unaffected. I chose this over a second slot. It is the one-design-per-person rule applied to the hire, and a hire can never lose its hand-back. The cost is that a second design waits for the first hire, typically seconds to minutes; Duplicate still works meanwhile.
- **NS2. Big edits survive a close.** The close flush is now an ordinary save, with no size cap. Only `pagehide` uses `keepalive`. An edit over its 64 KiB cap sends the small fields over the server's soul and skills, and is kept in this browser's localStorage, keyed by design and expiring after 24 h. The next time New agent opens on that design, the edit is offered back and saved. It is never reported as saved before that. The same stash covers a reload that outruns its own keepalive save (NN4).
- **NS3. Retry follows the claim.** `POST /api/fleet/hires/{id}/retry` moves the design onto the retry's deterministic run id before it enqueues, whether the design is still held or was already handed back from that hire (`released_from`). The design is spent when the retry finishes.
- **NS4. A stale tab's Create.** Create names the design *before* its flush. If the flush meets a newer design, Create stops. A 409 from the hire refetches and reseeds the form, so a design id never leaves with a form from an older revision.
- **The S7 gap.** The hire route now goes through `talaria_agent_design::gate_hire` (claim → enqueue → release on failure). Four tests pin that order; consuming the design after the enqueue cannot be written through it.
- **NN1:** Duplicate no longer marks the design as watched.
- **NN3:** Discard clears a pending save.
- **Verified:**
  - `cargo test -p talaria-agent-design --lib -- --include-ignored`: 36 passed, including the live NS1 and NS3 tests and the `gate_hire` tests.
  - ui: 21 tests in `lib/agent-design.test.ts` (held, keepalive body cap, stash restore and expiry).
  - `bun run gate` passed.
  - Headless Chromium on the worktree stack:
    - NS1: opened on "Hiring Scout"; a describe and a manual save were each refused with 409; after the hire failed, the modal moved to review with the reason.
    - NS3: a failed hire with a real input was retried through the route; the design followed, was spent, and the agent `retry92719` exists.
    - NS4: with and without a pending edit, the stale tab showed the current design, no hire went out from it, and the newer design was untouched.
  - These headless runs found two bugs, both fixed in `6bb6a953`: an open modal stayed on describe after a held design came back, and a conflict refetch did not reseed the form.

## Fix verification round 4 (NS5–NS8)

- **NS5: New agent stays open during a hire.** The hire's claim now moves the design out of the person's slot into `agent-design:<user>:hires`, a hash of held designs keyed by design id. The move is one Lua script: compare-and-set on the slot's revision, then HSET and DEL. The slot is free at once, so the next design can be started while the first one boots. Settling happens on read, the same way as before:
  - **Hire finished:** the design is used up.
  - **Hire failed before the agent existed:**
    - *Slot empty:* the design goes back into the slot, on review, with the hire's reason. A second Lua script only writes an empty slot.
    - *Slot occupied:* the design **waits**. It never overwrites the design the person started meanwhile. A bell row reads "The hire of <name> did not finish", and New agent shows a line with **Discard it**. Once the open design is hired or discarded, the returned one moves into the slot.
  - This was the simplest shape I found that loses nothing. GET now also answers `hiring` and `returned`, so the client follows the hires' run events and polls while a hire is in flight.
- **NS6:** when a design with a different id arrives (handed back, or started in another tab), the form refills from its draft, manual designs included. The one exception is the record created by this modal's own first save of a manual start.
- **NS7:** the kept pagehide edit is offered **once**, when the modal opens, whether the cache is cold or warm, and never from a 409's reseed. It is offered only while the server still holds the draft the edit was based on, or what its own keepalive sent. If something newer landed, the edit is dropped.
- **NS8:** a failed hire whose run checkpoint carries `defId` already made the agent, so the design is used up whatever failed after (download, boot, Start). Only failures before the agent exists hand the design back. Their sentence ("Check the fields and create it again") is then true.
- **NN6:** the stash is keyed per person (`talaria.agent-design.unsaved:<userId>`) and cleared at sign-out (`signOut` → `clearUnsavedEdits`).
- **NN7:** over the cap, the partial is sent only when it fits. If the saved soul is itself too large, nothing rides keepalive and only the stash keeps the edit.
- **NN8:** a save already in flight at pagehide is stashed too. Retry follows the design of the hire input's `managerUserId`, not the retrier's.
- **Wiring is pinned at the source:**
  - `the_hire_route_goes_through_the_design_gate` and `the_retry_route_takes_the_design_along_before_it_enqueues` (talaria-routes-fleet) fail if the hire route stops going through `gate_hire`, if it enqueues anywhere else, or if the retry route stops calling `follow_retry` before its enqueue.
  - `create-agent-modal-wiring.test.ts` fails if closing uses keepalive, if pagehide stops stashing, if the restore moves off the once-at-open path, or if Create stops naming its design before the flush.
- **Verified:**
  - `cargo test -p talaria-agent-design --lib -- --include-ignored`: 35 passed. The new live test `design_live_the_design_gates_the_hire_and_new_agent_stays_open` covers: a second claim refused; the slot empty during the hire; B started meanwhile; A failing, waiting with a bell row, and returning when B is discarded; and a hire that made the agent before its boot failed using the design up. Further live tests cover a waiting design being dismissed and a retry being followed.
  - The route wiring tests pass, and the ui suite passes (3071 tests). `bun run gate` passed.
  - Headless Chromium on the worktree stack:
    - **NS5:** New agent opened on describe during A's hire, and B was designed meanwhile. A's failure showed the waiting line and the bell row while the slot stayed B. Discarding B brought A back on review with its reason.
    - **NS6:** a returned *manual* design filled the form (Manny / manny / ops-m).
    - **NS7:** a kept edit was offered once on a warm cache, with the "Restored edits" note, then saved and removed. A second open did not offer it.
    - **NS8:** a hire that made the agent and then failed its boot used up the design, leaving nothing returned or hiring.
    - The NS5 run found one more bug, fixed before the commit: a discard did not ask for the design waiting behind it.
  - CI's live-tests failed once on `90d57243`. `design_live_refine_then_discard` raced the landing's bell re-alert. The race was in the test and had been there since the bell assertions were added. In `2011a05d`, `until_settled` waits for the design's run to finish as well as the record.
  - The `90d57243` subject is 90 characters, two over the 88 limit. It is pushed, so I left it unamended.

## Not verified
- The Cloudflare and traefik hops: there's no tunnel here. Nothing in this design depends on a held request.
- A reclaim after a real api crash mid-design: the runs runtime's sweep owns that path, and I didn't kill the api mid-run.
- Two api processes on one stack at once: the CAS script and the leases are what make that safe, and the live tests drive the store from separate connections, but I didn't run two api servers.
- Redis durability is RDB snapshots with no AOF (`docker/sidecars.compose.yml`): a Redis *crash* can lose designs written in the last minute or so. A clean stop saves them.
- A design whose api dies mid-run resumes when the 300 s lease expires, so the splash can count past five minutes first.
- The >64 KiB pagehide fallback (a partial keepalive save, or none, then the restore) is unit-tested, and the restore is exercised in a browser from a stash written the way pagehide writes it. A real keepalive over the cap was not driven, because Playwright's route interception does not catch unload-time keepalive requests. A tab closed outright on such an edit keeps it only in that browser.
- The headless runs used stand-in hires: a parked or erroring `runs` row, and a claim written into the hires hash the way the route's Lua writes it. The real claim → hire path is covered by the live tests and the earlier headless hire runs.
- The host disk stalled through this round (IO pressure 50–90%). One NS8 pass timed out its PG read, which counts as a live hire, and was re-run after the stall. One NS5 pass hit a headers timeout and was re-run.
- NN2: a `runs` insert that stalls more than 60 s (this host's known PG stalls) lets a read hand the claim back mid-commit. A second claim is then possible, normally stopped by the hire lock. This is rare, and I left it.
- Desktop and mobile shells. Bell rows reach them through the usual notification path.

Report-only audit of the other browser-held runs (13 findings; the top three are ticket Muse, KB Muse, and app install/update): `~/.claude/projects/…/release/durable-runs-audit.md`.

entries.title: fleet: agents search with the operator's chosen provider — one setting renders hermes's web backend
entries.body:
> **Merge order:** 2 of 14 — merge after #570; this branch already contains #570 and rc. It also restores the web-search key loop a previous rc merge dropped.

## What changed

Track **hx-web-search** of the Hermes-overlap rollout (research-eval "Phase B"). Agents now search the web with a provider the operator picks, through their own Hermes. Research keeps its own search stage and does not read this setting.

- **One org setting:** `agent_web_search`, in the new crate `talaria-agent-web-search`, edited at **Admin → Search → Agent web search** (`GET/PUT /api/admin/search/agents`). It holds:
  - `backend`: empty means Hermes's own default.
  - an optional `extractBackend` for reading pages.
  - one sealed key per picked vendor.
  - `allowKeylessPublicTiers`.
- **The render** (`talaria-fleet-render`) writes:
  - `web.search_backend`, and `web.extract_backend` when one is set, merged into each agent's own `web:` block.
  - the vendor key: unsealed into `fleet/.env` as `TALARIA_WEB_<VAR>`, then interpolated into the service under the exact env name the Hermes provider reads. The value never lands in the compose file or config.yaml.
  - `web.keyless_fallback: false` and `web.keyless_rescue: false` whenever a backend is picked, or the search URL is rendered into the agents as `SEARXNG_URL`, unless the operator allowed the public tiers. Rendered is not reachable: nothing probes the URL from an agent.
  - nothing at all when nothing is set.
  - a **render warning** when reading pages is left to Hermes and its `web_extract` autodetect would land on a search-only backend (Brave Search, or SearXNG through `SEARXNG_URL`). Every `web_extract` then fails with Hermes's typed error.
- **The org choice wins** over an agent's own `web.search_backend` / `extract_backend` / `keyless_*` and over a per-agent secret named like the vendor key (compose `environment:` beats `env_file:`). The user doc says so.
- **Backends offered,** each checked against Hermes v0.22.4 `plugins/web/<vendor>/provider.py` (NAME, KEY_ENV, EXTRACT, KEYLESS). A unit test pins the table.

  | Backend | Key env | Reads pages | Without a key |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | `tavily` | `TAVILY_API_KEY` | yes | public tier |
  | `exa` | `EXA_API_KEY` | yes | public tier |
  | `parallel` | `PARALLEL_API_KEY` | yes | public tier |
  | `firecrawl` | `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | yes | keyless cloud |
  | `keenable` | `KEENABLE_API_KEY` | yes | public tier |
  | `perplexity` | `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` | yes | fails |
  | `brave-free` | `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY` | no | fails |
  | `searxng` | `SEARXNG_URL`, from the workspace search URL | no | n/a |

- **Validation:** `PUT` refuses:
  - an unknown backend.
  - a search-only backend for reading pages.
  - a key for a vendor that is not picked.
  - a key that a `.env` line could not hold.
  - a keyed vendor with no key, unless its anonymous tier is allowed.
  - Perplexity or Brave with no key at all.
  - SearXNG with no search URL.

  Switching vendors drops the old key. The write audits as `search.agents_configure`, recording vendor names only. Read, apply and write run in one transaction under `select … for update` on the setting row, the lock DEK rotation takes too, so concurrent saves or a save racing a rotation cannot write back a stale copy.
- **Secrets plumbing:** the key shows in the secrets inventory (`setting:agent_web_search:keys.<vendor>`, clearable) and is re-sealed by DEK rotation, per docs/ENCRYPTION.md.
- **UI:** Admin gains a **Search** tab. It carries the new panel, plus a search URL editor for the existing `/api/admin/search`, which had no UI. Picks autosave. A keyed vendor without a stored key is held as a draft until its key is saved, and then both land together. The copy states the split: agents use this provider through Hermes, while research uses the search URL or a registered search MCP server. The "Agents get:" line and the warnings under it come from the server's own render: the GET returns `rendered` (`web` keys, env names, `searxngUrl`, `warnings`). The panel no longer re-derives the rules.
- **One rule for the search URL:** `agent_search_url` and `dial_is_container` moved unchanged from `talaria-fleet-render` into `talaria-fleet-layout`, with their test. The render and the Admin → Search read-back both call them.
- **Docs:** ARCHITECTURE (search paragraph), ENCRYPTION (sealed-value list), user/admin-agents, and the regenerated `docs/api/admin.md`.

## Verified

On this worktree's stack, with an agent on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69201726bc…` image. Every read-back below came from inside the container, as the `hermes` user, from `/opt/hermes`: `/opt/data/config.yaml`, the container env, and Hermes's own `tools.web_tools` resolution functions.

| Case | What the container had, and what Hermes did |
| :--- | :--- |
| Nothing set | No `web:` block and no vendor key in env. `_get_search_backend()` landed on the keyless ring (firecrawl, then keenable). Keyless tier and rescue on. |
| Tavily plus a test key | Config read `search_backend: tavily`, `keyless_fallback: false`, `keyless_rescue: false`, and `TAVILY_API_KEY` equalled the saved key. Hermes resolved `tavily` with the tier and rescue off. `web_search` reached `api.tavily.com` and returned Tavily's `Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key.` with no rescue. |
| The same, as a real chat turn | Sent on the agent's API server, with the LLM going through the gateway (Z.ai `glm-4.7-flash`). Hermes's `agent.log` shows `Web search via tavily: 'Hermes Agent project Nous Research'`. The agent replied: *The tool returned an error: "Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key."* |
| Public tiers allowed | The keyless keys were not rendered. The same failed Tavily call came back `rescued_from: tavily` with three results from the keyless ring. That is the fallthrough the default now prevents. |
| Search URL alone | `SEARXNG_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8888` plus both keyless switches. Hermes resolved `searxng` with no rescue. |
| SearXNG search, Firecrawl page reading | Both rendered, with `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` from the `.env`. Hermes resolved search to `searxng` and extract to `firecrawl`. |
| Cleared | The `web:` block, the compose variable and the `.env` line were all gone, and the setting row's keys were `{}`. |
| Terminal scrub | Hermes's `_sanitize_subprocess_env` drops `TAVILY_API_KEY` and `EXA_API_KEY` from terminal children. They are `tool` entries in its OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS. |
| PUT refusals | All seven refusal cases above returned 400 with their sentence, and a non-object `keys` was refused too. |
| Rotation | `POST /api/admin/encryption` re-sealed the key from `v2:1:` to `v2:2:` (`reencrypted: 2`). The next render delivered the identical value. |
| Secrets inventory | Lists `Agent web search key (tavily)`, state `ok`, href `/admin/search`. |
| UI | A headless browser on `/admin/search` picked Tavily with no key. The draft note showed, Save key committed both, and the summary read `search: tavily · TAVILY_API_KEY sealed · keyless tiers off`. |
| Brave only, nothing for pages (review follow-up) | The PUT response's `rendered.warnings` and `POST /api/fleet/render`'s `result.warnings` both carried the search-only warning. In the recreated container, `_get_extract_backend()` resolved `brave-free` and `web_extract` returned `Brave Search (Free) is a search-only backend and cannot extract URL content`. |
| The same, public tiers allowed | Keyless switches not rendered; extract still resolved `brave-free` and failed the same way. Autodetect runs before the keyless walk. |
| Brave search, Firecrawl pages | `rendered.warnings` was `[]`; the container resolved extract to `firecrawl`. |
| Search URL alone | Warning naming SearXNG. Extract resolved `searxng` and `web_extract` failed with `SearXNG is a search-only backend`. The same happened with the public tiers allowed, so no `web:` block at all, which is exactly the pre-PR render. |
| Panel | Admin → Search showed `Agents get: SEARXNG_URL · keyless tiers off`, with the warning under it, both read from the GET's `rendered`. |
| Row lock | A psql session took `select … for update` on the row, changed `allowKeylessPublicTiers`, and held the lock for 6 s. A PUT sent 1 s in returned after 6.7 s and kept the holder's change. Without the lock, that change would have been overwritten. |
| Refusals under the lock | A refused PUT left `updated_at` unchanged. A refused first save, with the row deleted beforehand, left no row behind. |

`bun run gate` passed (re-run after the review follow-up):
- check
- ui svelte-check (0 errors) and vitest (1,887, including `search.test.ts`)
- fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for the seven touched api packages, including 17 `talaria-agent-web-search` tests

CI is the full-workspace proof, because `Cargo.lock` moved with the new crate.

Not exercised live: a real vendor answering with results under a real key (I hold no vendor key, so every keyed call used a test key and proved routing and auth only), and keyed Exa, Parallel or Firecrawl inside a running agent. Their SDKs are not in the v0.22.4 image. A throwaway container showed `pm.ensure_import("exa")` installing the SDK and then asking for a Hermes restart; the panel says so for those three.

## Decisions for the reviewer

1. **A search URL alone now switches Hermes's keyless tiers off.** This follows the plan's spec. The condition is that the URL is *rendered* as `SEARXNG_URL`, not that it is reachable: nothing probes it from an agent, and the code, the docs and the changelog now all say exactly that. An install whose `SEARXNG_URL` cannot answer from agent containers loses the silent rescue through third parties, and agents get SearXNG's own error instead. This dev host is an example, because its `talaria-searxng-dev` is published on 127.0.0.1 only, so `host.docker.internal:8888` is refused (shown above). The checkbox restores the old behaviour. The conservative alternative is to count only a picked backend, not a search URL. That is a one-line change in `render()`.
7. **A search-only backend left to read pages is a warning, not a refusal** (review follow-up). Brave Search and SearXNG cannot extract, and with `web.extract_backend` unset Hermes's `web_extract` autodetect lands on them. Refusing the save would block SearXNG-only, which is a legitimate keyless setup. It would also be inconsistent, because a bare search URL already sends `web_extract` to SearXNG today, with or without this PR (verified above). So the render warns, in the render route, hire logs and the Admin → Search panel, and names the fix: pick a provider under Read pages.
8. **The org choice overrides per-agent settings:** the agent def's own `web.search_backend` / `extract_backend` / `keyless_*`, and a per-agent secret named like the vendor key (compose `environment:` beats `env_file:`). The user doc now says so. Refusing Hermes-reserved names at hire is #572's territory.
2. **The key is sealed into the setting row,** like the email transport and reranker keys. It is not a reference to a workspace Secrets vault doc, because vault docs are handles agents use without reading, while this value has to be rendered into the container env.
3. **Three v0.22.4 backends are left out:** `ddgs` (the package is not in the image, and Hermes installs it only from its interactive picker), `xai` (a model call to x.ai on `XAI_API_KEY`, outside the gateway), and `openai-native` (it needs the Codex Responses transport and OAuth).
4. **The write rolls nothing.** This is the toolset floor's rule: the choice lands on each agent at its next render or roll, and the panel says so. The vendor key rides the container environment, so a running agent always needs a recreate.
5. **Keys are limited to `[A-Za-z0-9._~:+/=-]`,** because they land as one unquoted line in the compose `--env-file`, which interpolates `$` and strips `#` comments. The render re-checks after unsealing.
6. **The Search URL editor is added to the new tab.** It is not strictly in the track, but the endpoint existed with no UI, and picking SearXNG depends on it.

## Merge order and dependencies

- Standalone. A freshly created or recreated agent reads all of this at boot.
- A config-only change (for example the keyless switch) reaches an already-running container once **#574 (hx-rolls)** lands, because of the inode fix. Until then it needs a recreate. I hit exactly this while exercising: `up` did not recreate when only config.yaml changed, so I used stop then up.
- Textual overlap with the other hx tracks in `talaria-fleet-render/src/lib.rs`:
  - The read before the loop.
  - One `merge_into` line after `fleet_disabled_toolsets`. It sits next to lines that #568, #570 and #572 add.
  - The env insert beside `SEARXNG_URL`. **#566 (hx-chain-gate)** deletes the `TALARIA_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` insert directly below it, so whichever merges second resolves a trivial conflict there. Keep both sides: this PR's loop and #566's deletion.
  - The review follow-up deletes `dial_is_container` / `agent_search_url` from fleet-render (moved to `talaria-fleet-layout`) and puts a `use` at their old spot. No other open hx PR touches those lines, and the imports block #572 edits is left alone.
  - #574's `render_fleet(pg, sb)` signature change does not touch any of these.
- Research-eval Phase A (hx-dead-code) is independent.

entries.body:
## Why

Talaria's top bar becomes the playground's Chrome tab bar. The open view is a tab cut from the page surface, and every other view is a small icon tile. Later, a view an agent is working in shows a core waiting glyph, drawn only from a real server signal. This PR is T1 of that program: the bar itself, with no glyphs, no readout and no tab-switch motion (T3 and T4 stack on this branch).

## What changed

- `TabBar.svelte` replaces `TopDock.svelte`, which is deleted. `dockSections`, `manageArea`, `navActiveItem`, `useNavBadges` and `useEnabledApps` move over verbatim, so who sees which item, the badges, and the right cluster's order (apps-broken retry, assistant, gear, divider, search, bell, account chip) are unchanged.
- The open item is drawn as the Chrome tab. It has the page's colour and its icon and label, and its feet curve out over the bar's bottom hairline. It carries `aria-current="page"`. Every other item is an `h-8 w-8` icon tile, an `<a href>` with `RailTooltip` and its badge.
- Settings and Admin still light the account chip, and the manage area still lights the gear. Neither gets a tab.
- The mark is 28px, and the TALARIA wordmark shows from the bar's `@4xl` container width up.
- At narrow widths the strip scrolls sideways. `lib/tab-strip.ts`'s `edgeFade` shows a trailing fade only while tabs remain to the right.
- The tab shape and the fade live in `styles.css`. The plan names `app.css`, but the repo has no such file.
- `NavIcon` takes an optional `size`. Each tab's icon renders through one `face` snippet, the slot T3 swaps for `TabFace`.

## Verified

- **Gate:** `bun run gate` passes: check, svelte-check (0 errors), vitest (190 files, 2962 tests).
- **Unit:** `bun run test -- tab-strip` asserts `data-more` while tabs remain to the right, cleared at the end of the scroll.
- **Exercised:** live lanes in progress. Screenshots and the review video will be added here.

## Branch flow

No.

## CHANGELOG entry

See `changelog/2026-11-03-tab-bar-replaces-top-dock.md`.

entries.title: api: serve which views an agent is working in (T2)
entries.body:
## Why

Talaria's top bar is becoming a Chrome-style tab bar. A view an agent is working in shows a waiting glyph, and only a real server signal may light it. No read answered "which view is an agent working in". This PR adds that read, `GET /api/working`, and the client query `useWorking()`. It has no UI. T3 draws the glyphs from it.

## What changed

- `GET /api/working` answers `{ comms, work, boards }`. Each arm is `{ count, label, href }` for the freshest working item, or null when nothing is working there.
- Each arm reuses its engine's own predicate instead of a copy:
  - the conversation list's `working` flag and audience;
  - the room page's 15-minute dead-stream silence;
  - the research status projection;
  - board visibility with the board's work-session join.

  The conversation list and the unread badges now share those spellings (`audience_sql!`, `working_sql!`, `rail_room_sql!`, `dead_stream_sql!`, `VIEWER_AUDIENCE`).
- `ui/src/lib/working.svelte.ts` holds `useWorking()`. It is one query, invalidated on firehose `run`, `conversation` and `channel` events. It polls every 5s while anything is lit and every 30s when idle. A failed read, including a failed refetch, reads as null.

## Scope

- Comms counts your streaming chats and your rail rooms with a streaming agent reply.
- Work counts streaming work, plan and research threads, plus research runs that are queued or running.
- Boards counts tickets on boards you can see that have a work session queued or running. Boards ships with an arm, because its predicate exists. The perf lane checks its cost.
- A run parked on a question (`awaiting`) is waiting on a person, so it does not count.
- Knowledge, Files and apps have no arm, so nothing can light them.

## Tradeoffs

- **Not folded into `/api/unreads`.** Unreads counts what has already landed, on a 30s floor. Working flips within seconds and fails for different reasons.
- **Polls while lit.** Room replies and ticket sessions send no firehose event when they end, so a lit arm needs its own pace to clear. That pace is 5s, the same as the sidebar's and the ticket ticker's.

## Blast Radius

The conversation list, the room list and both unread badges now read their audience from the shared macros. The SQL text is the same apart from one change: the channel unread count moved `archived_at is null` from its join to its WHERE, which is equivalent for an inner join. The gate's crate tests and the existing live tests pass.

## Verification

- `bun run gate` passes. It ran check, the ui typecheck, 2961 ui tests, and clippy and tests for the six touched crates.
- Live-DB tests (`cargo test -p talaria-routes-comms --lib -- --ignored working_live`) cover three cases:
  - a streaming chat reply lights Comms with its title and link, and stops counting once silent past 5 minutes;
  - a room reply does the same, with a 15-minute window;
  - another person's chat never counts.
- `ui/src/lib/working.test.ts` checks that a 500 reads as null, never as "nothing working", and that a failed refetch drops the old reading.

entries.body:
FB13b: the CI and tooling follow-ups that waited for #651, #652, #654 and #657, plus one release-day bug the coordinator added: GitHub's "Latest" release.

## The release-day bug: a stable server release would take the desktop updater feed

**Root cause.** The desktop updater reads `https://github.com/outcrop-labs/talaria/releases/latest/download/latest.json` (`desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`). So GitHub's Latest release is the feed, and today that is `desktop-v0.11.0`. `release.yml` ran `gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag …` for a stable `vX.Y.Z` with no Latest flag, and GitHub makes a new non-prerelease release Latest by default. The first stable tag (v0.13.0) would have moved Latest to a release that has no `latest.json` until desktop-package.yml's `attach` job finishes (that job runs after `publish`), and has none at all if a desktop job fails. Every installed app's update check would have 404'd. desktop-package.yml's mint also relied on the default, which made it Latest when it was created, before its `latest.json` was uploaded.

**Fix.**
- `release.yml`: the stable and RC create, and the re-run's edit, all say `--latest=false`.
- `desktop-package.yml`: the `desktop-vX.Y.0` mint is created `--latest=false`, and `Upload` marks it Latest with `gh release edit "$TAG" --latest`, after `latest.json` is up. The feed now really does flip last, as the file's comments already said.
- The guard is `scripts/release-latest.mjs`, run by `check-invariants.mjs` as `release-latest-is-the-desktop-feed`, with a 12-fixture self-test. It fails a dropped `--latest=false` on either release.yml call, a mint left to the default, a Latest flip placed before the `latest.json` upload, any other workflow marking a release Latest, and any `gh release create` that states neither `--prerelease` nor a flag. It also fails if the updater endpoint stops reading `/releases/latest`, because the rule depends on that.
- RELEASING.md, the cut-release skill and docs/DESKTOP.md now say the server release is never Latest, because the desktop feed is. The desktop-package.yml header no longer says installed apps update themselves: they read the feed when someone clicks Check for updates.

**Consequence to know.** A `vX.Y.Z` release still carries the desktop installers and a `latest.json`, but nothing serves that file. Installed apps stay on the newest `desktop-v*` release until the next desktop mint, which counts the `v*` tags (after v0.13.0, desktop-v0.14.0).

## The follow-ups

1. **FB9b: #651's compensating git-hosts SQL is run, not only applied.** A new migrations-job step runs `ui/scripts/check-git-hosts-mirror.sql` on both scratch databases, inside a transaction it rolls back. It checks:
   - `DEFAULT 'github'` on `host_id` in `workbench_repos`, `workbench_repo_flow`, `workbench_jobs` and `workbench_repo_requests`, plus an insert that names no host;
   - at rest, `github_config` equals the `github` row with its orgs folded back in;
   - a row write rewrites the setting;
   - a setting write, in main's own `set_setting` upsert shape, rewrites the row on both its INSERT and UPDATE paths, and the setting keeps what was written;
   - a row delete empties the setting, and a later setting write makes the row again.

   The upgrade pass now seeds a connected GitHub (main's shape, placeholder values) on main's schema before this branch's array runs. The check then requires the config to come through the move and back unchanged. The file's header says to delete it with the contract release that drops the mirrors.
2. **The connect smoke runs on the installed apps.**
   - Windows: on the exe the NSIS or MSI installer put on the runner. Its path goes through `GITHUB_ENV`, and the 20 s run's whole tree is killed first with `taskkill /T`.
   - macOS: on the binary inside the shipped `.app`.
   - Linux: on the binary the deb installed through apt. The package name and binary path are read from the deb, and the run uses `xvfb-run` with `dbus-run-session`.

   All three pass `--force`, because the runner is thrown away and earlier launches may have written the registry. The AppImage is not run, since it bundles its own libraries.
3. **#654: tests for the two re-check `if`s in `removeArtifact`.** In each, a checkout or a `.talaria-keep` appears after the scan:
   - an orphan `talaria-wt-*` project gets a checkout, and an orphan `devbox-*` project gets a keep;
   - a stack, a worktree and a box each get a keep.

   `docker` and `git` are stand-ins on PATH, and a probe proves they answer before anything runs. Each refusal is paired with the same row going ahead once nothing is in its way.
4. **#657 review shoulds.**
   - (a) The e2e surface is now `api/crates/*`, `api/src/*`, the manifest, the lockfile, `api/.cargo/*` and the toolchain pin. The root package depends on all 243 workspace crates (218 directly), so the old list was incomplete for shared crates. The comment says why, and docs/E2E.md matches. Cost: e2e runs on every Rust PR, alongside the api job, which takes longer.
   - (b) The notes link is `blob/main/CHANGELOG.md`, not the tag, and the docs now say so.
   - (c) A stable rolls under its own version. If the roll refuses because `changelog/` is empty right after an RC, skip the roll.
   - (d) Stale comments fixed: the `release.yml` header, and `mobile/androidApp/build.gradle.kts:11`.
5. **gate.mjs.** Its ui list now is ci.yml's ui surface (`UI_SURFACE`), and `--self-test` reads ci.yml and fails when the two differ. The dither engine also runs the desktop typecheck, as ci.yml's desktop surface does.

## How it was verified

- **Latest flags.**
  - gh 2.102.0 was pointed at a local fake GitHub API (a throwaway TLS cert; nothing reached GitHub). release.yml's create and edit sent `make_latest: "false"` for both the stable and the RC. The mint sent `"false"`, and the flip sent `"true"`. A create with no flag sent no `make_latest`, which GitHub treats as Latest.
  - Each flag was dropped from the real workflows in turn, and `check-invariants.mjs` failed and named the line every time: the edit, the create, the mint, the flip, and the flip moved above the upload.
- **Mirror check.** It ran on two throwaway postgres:16 containers: a fresh replay (537 statements), and main's array (459) with GitHub seeded, followed by this branch's (78).
  - It passed on both and left the data unchanged, and the replay afterwards applied 0.
  - It failed, with a message naming what it saw, for each of nine breakages: the default dropped on `workbench_jobs` or on `workbench_repo_flow`, either trigger dropped, the delete branch gone, the setting trigger on UPDATE only, the copy-back missing, the setting drifted from the row, and a baseline differing from the seed.
- **Sweep tests.** They pass under bun and node, and each fails when its `if` is removed from a scratch copy of the sweep. The sweep itself was never run.
- **Surfaces.** ci.yml's `changes` matcher was extracted and run on single files, against rc and against this branch. `talaria-db`, `-state`, `-kb`, `api/.cargo/config.toml` and `api/rust-toolchain.toml` now run e2e, while `api/tests/` and `api/package.Dockerfile` still don't. The gate's self-test fails with a ui entry removed.
- **desktop-package.yml and release.yml.** These cannot run from a pull request, and nothing was dispatched.
  - Both were parsed (Bun's YAML), and every bash step passed `bash -n`.
  - `connect-smoke.mjs` was run as the new steps call it, against a stand-in shell at a path with spaces. It refused an existing registry without `--force` and passed with it. It named the hang when the page was never requested, failed a crash right after the open, and stopped on an empty `INSTALLED_EXE`.
- **Gates.** `bun run check` passes. `bun run gate` ran `check`, the ui svelte-check (0 errors in 5704 files) and the ui tests (2954 passed), then stopped at its mobile step: the comment edit in `build.gradle.kts` selects gradle, and this host has no JDK.

## Not verified

- The installed-app smoke on real runners. desktop-package.yml first runs on the promotion push to main, or in release.yml's call on the next tag. If a platform's installed build cannot open the fake instance there, that job goes red before anything is attached, which is the point of the step. The likeliest surprise is a runner-specific one, such as how the deb installs.
- `gh release edit --latest` against real GitHub. Only the payload gh sends was checked.
- The mobile gradle build for the comment-only edit in `build.gradle.kts`. This host has no JDK, so CI's mobile job is that gate.
- actionlint: it could not be fetched in this session.
