entries.title: apps: server-side code can import zod again — the same copy the sdk re-exports as z (FB3)
entries.body:
# Pull request

**Base branch: `rc`.** Release-sweep batch FB3, release blocker **B3**, ahead of the rc → main promotion (#597).

## Checklist

- [x] This PR targets `rc`.
- [x] `bun run gate` is green locally. It compiles only what this diff touches; CI runs the full surface job.
- [x] I exercised the changed path in the running app; the steps are under **Verified**.
- [x] A [`changelog/`](../changelog/) file, `changelog/2026-11-02-apps-import-zod.md`, carries what changed and what was verified.
- [x] Generated files were regenerated, not hand-edited (none are touched).

## What changed

**Sweep finding fixed:** `apps-2`, release blocker B3. Apps whose server-side code imports `zod` are refused by rc's app build. This is a regression from main.

### What broke

- On rc, `import { z } from 'zod'` in `server.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `harnesses/` or a `lib/schema.ts` they import fails the build: `"zod" is not shared with apps: an app has no node_modules of its own where it is installed, so a server-side module may import only @talaria/sdk/server (which re-exports zod as z) and node's builtins`.
- This release moves `BUILD_RECIPE` to 4, so every installed app rebuilds at the first boot after the upgrade. A failed build drops the app from `apps_enabled` (`failHealth`, audited as `app.disable` by `system:app-health`). So an app that imports zod would be **turned off by the upgrade**.
- The owner's `apps/leadworks` (27ed858) and `apps/waypoint` (2fad387) both import zod from `lib/schema.ts`. Both fail rc's SDK kit build with that sentence. They were read through scratch clones and never edited.
- In dev, where an app's server-side code loads from source, an install failed `server failed to load: Cannot find module 'zod'`, and an update that added a zod import rolled back with the same error.

### Root cause

- Main's `docs/sdk/README.md` said svelte, svelte-query, **zod** and `@lucide/svelte` "all resolve from the host", and main's in-host build bundled zod.
- #589 made `build.ts` refuse every bare import the host does not share (`talaria-app-shared-imports-only`). The server side shared only `@talaria/sdk/server`. zod is the module the SDK re-exports as `z`, but it was never a shared specifier, so the refusal caught it with everything else.
- The server chunks also linked every server specifier to the one SDK shim (`paths: () => shim`). There was no runtime file a bare `zod` could link to.
- In dev, Vite externalizes a bare `zod` for SSR and node-resolves it from the importer's directory. `apps/` sits outside `ui/`, so it found nothing. The kit's typecheck mapped no `zod` either, so `talaria-app check` failed with "Cannot find module 'zod'".

### Fix

zod becomes a shared server package beside `@talaria/sdk/server`, the same module the SDK re-exports, linked and never bundled.

- `ui/src/app-runtime/specifiers.ts`: `SHARED_SERVER_PACKAGES = ['zod']` joins `serverSpecifiers()`. `serverRuntimeFile(id)` maps each server specifier to its own `rt-*.js`, by exact match: `zod/mini` throws, naming the import. `shimSource` adds `export { default }` for zod, so `import z from 'zod'` works too. `bundledShared` flags a zod bundled into an app chunk.
- `ui/src/app-runtime/vite-plugin.ts`: the host build writes `dist/server/runtime/rt-zod.js` from `shimSource`, beside `rt-talaria-sdk-server.js`. Both import the host's one external zod.
- `ui/src/server/app-build/build.ts`: `unsharedImport` lets a bare `zod` through in server-side code. A zod value import in a surface gets its own sentence: shared with server-side modules only, and a surface takes the types by `import type`. Server, mcp and harness chunks link each shared specifier to its own runtime file. The test seam `setServerShim(path)` becomes `setServerShims(dir)`.
- `ui/vite.config.ts`: `resolve.dedupe` adds zod, so in dev an app file outside `ui/` resolves the host's copy, as svelte already does.
- SDK kit (`ui/scripts/build-sdk-kit.ts`, `ui/src/sdk-kit/kit.ts`, `ui/src/sdk-kit/check.ts`): the kit ships `rt-zod.js` in the same `Bun.build` as the SDK shim, so they share one zod. `check` typechecks the bare `zod` entry (no `zod/*`) and maps it to that shim in the app's vitest config.
- Docs: `docs/sdk/README.md`, `docs/sdk/outside-the-host.md` and the comment in `ui/src/sdk/server.ts` now state the rule. The example refusal is now `"clsx" is not shared with apps`.
- The refusal of every other unshared package is unchanged.

**Files beyond the batch's expected six.** Each is named here, as the batch asks:

- `ui/src/app-runtime/vite-plugin.ts`: it writes the host's runtime shims. Without `rt-zod.js` there is nothing to link to.
- `ui/vite.config.ts`: this is the dev half of the bug (the rolled-back update).
- `ui/scripts/build-sdk-kit.ts`, `ui/src/sdk-kit/kit.ts`, `ui/src/sdk-kit/check.ts`: the kit runs the host's recipe. Without these, `talaria-app build` and `check` would still refuse what the host accepts.
- `ui/src/sdk/server.ts`: a comment only. It said apps cannot import zod.
- `ui/src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts`: the new tests for the specifier rules and the dev resolution.
- `scripts/skills/talaria-apps/SKILL.md` and `references/lifecycle.md` are listed in the report's batch table. The judge asks about them because `scripts/skills/` is product surface. That is why they change: the shipped `talaria-apps` skill tells Hermes agents that zod is refused and quotes that refusal as its example. Left alone, it would steer agent-written apps away from what the SDK supports.

## Verified

- **Gate:** `bun run gate` passed after merging `origin/rc` at 346c222b (#643–#646, no conflicts, none of them touch these files). It ran check, then svelte-check on 5702 files with 0 errors and 0 warnings, then the ui vitest suite: 189 files, 2927 tests, all passing. The first gate run had passed every test, but it failed one file-level hook: `src/sdk/client-docs.test.ts`'s `afterAll` `rmSync` of its scratch workspace hit vitest's 10 s hook timeout during a host IO stall (`/proc/pressure/io` full avg10 ≈ 60%). That test reads `client.md`, `ui-kit.md`, `getting-started.md`, `mcp.md` and `apps/README.md`, none of which this PR edits. It passed on the re-run, unchanged.
- **Judge:** `node scripts/judge-pr.mjs --base origin/rc` reported 0 must, 0 should, 1 ask: the `scripts/skills/` edits, argued above.
- **Tests that fail on the old code.** The new tests were run against rc 65dbae86's source in a scratch tree. 14 fail there. In `build.test.ts` and `sdk-kit.test.ts`, 10 of 49 fail:

  ```
  FAIL  src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > builds an app whose server, tools and harness import zod, linking it to the host runtime and bundling none
  AssertionError: expected '[commonjs--resolver] [plugin talaria-…' to be null
  FAIL  src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > loads the built server with one zod: z from the SDK and zod itself, named, whole and default, are one module
  AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { named: true, namespace: true, …(4) }
  FAIL  src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > refuses a subpath of zod, which the host does not share, naming it
  FAIL  src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > refuses zod in a surface — a value import from the module that uses it — saying a type comes in by `import type`
  FAIL  src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > unsharedImport > lets paths, schemes and the shared specifiers through, per kind
  AssertionError: zod: expected '"zod" is not shared with apps: an app…' to be null
  FAIL  src/sdk-kit/sdk-kit.test.ts > check > typechecks against the kit: the SDK entries and the shared packages, and nothing else
  AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal [ '/kit/node_modules/zod' ]
  …
   Test Files  3 failed (3)
        Tests  10 failed | 39 passed (49)
  ```

  In `specifiers.test.ts`, 4 fail. Among them is the dev server test, which fails on rc's `vite.config.ts` with the live symptom:

  ```
  FAIL  src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > server specifiers > share zod beside the SDK, each with its own runtime file
  AssertionError: expected [ '@talaria/sdk/server' ] to deeply equal [ '@talaria/sdk/server', 'zod' ]
  FAIL  src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > the dev server resolves an app's server-side zod to the host's > gives an app file imported after the host the same zod
  Error: Cannot find module 'zod' imported from '/tmp/dev-zod-jygoZo/apps/notes/server.ts'
  ```

  On this branch, the same files pass:

  ```
  ✓ src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > server specifiers > share zod beside the SDK, each with its own runtime file
  ✓ src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > server specifiers > share no subpath of zod, naming the import
  ✓ src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > server specifiers > flag a bundled zod as a shared module leaked into an app chunk
  ✓ src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > shimSource > carries zod's default too: `import z from 'zod'` is the same namespace as `{ z }`
  ✓ src/app-runtime/specifiers.test.ts > the dev server resolves an app's server-side zod to the host's > gives an app file imported after the host the same zod
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > unsharedImport > lets paths, schemes and the shared specifiers through, per kind
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > unsharedImport > says a server-side package is the server side's, and how a surface takes its types
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (a package the app does not get) > refuses a server-side import of a package the host does not share, even where it resolves
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > builds an app whose server, tools and harness import zod, linking it to the host runtime and bundling none
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > loads the built server with one zod: z from the SDK and zod itself, named, whole and default, are one module
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > refuses a subpath of zod, which the host does not share, naming it
  ✓ src/server/app-build/build.test.ts > buildApp (zod, shared with server-side code) > refuses zod in a surface — a value import from the module that uses it — saying a type comes in by `import type`
  ✓ src/sdk-kit/sdk-kit.test.ts > check > typechecks against the kit: the SDK entries and the shared packages, and nothing else
  ✓ src/sdk-kit/sdk-kit.test.ts > check > runs the app's tests with the SDK entries mapped exactly, so '@talaria/sdk' never takes '/server'
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
       Tests  64 passed (64)
  ```

- **Reproduced on rc 65dbae86 first.** The rc SDK kit's `talaria-app build` of a fixture whose `lib/schema.ts`, `server.ts` and `mcp.ts` import zod (named, `* as` and default) failed with `"zod" is not shared with apps`. Its `talaria-app check` failed with 5 "Cannot find module 'zod'" errors. The rc kit's build of leadworks and of waypoint failed the same way, with `exit 1`.
- **Exercised: dev stack** (`rel-apps` worktree, slot 9: app :5309, api :5409, the prebuilt rc api).
  - Before, on rc: a fresh install of the fixture built `failed` with `server failed to load: Cannot find module 'zod' imported from …`. Updating an installed copy from the plain commit to the zod commit rolled back.
  - After: the same update applied (`"rolledBack":false`, build `ready`). The fresh install rebuilt `ready` and was enabled. Its route reported `{"named":true,"namespace":true,"default":true,"instance":true,"parsed":true,"refused":false}`, meaning zod's named, namespace and default imports are the SDK's `z` and `instanceof` holds across them. `parseBody` with the app's own zod schema answered 400 `Too small: expected string to have >=1 characters` for `{"title":""}`, and 200 with the defaults filled for `{"title":"hello"}`.
- **Exercised: production server.** The host was built from the branch with `bun run build`. It emits `dist/server/runtime/rt-zod.js`, and zod stays external in both shims. `ui/server-entry.ts` rebuilt the fixture with a `server.js` that imports only `…/runtime/rt-talaria-sdk-server.js` and `…/runtime/rt-zod.js`, with no zod bundled (0 `$ZodObject` in the app's `server.js`). It served the same identity report.
- **Exercised: an upgrade's first boot.** The host build id was changed and the production server rebooted. The boot sweep then rebuilt every installed app under the new key, each `ready`: the two fixtures (`app.js`, `app.css`, `server.js`, `mcp.js`) and a leadworks install (`server.js`, `mcp.js`, `harnesses.js`). The enabled fixture still answered 400 and 200 as above.
- **Exercised: the SDK kit built from the branch.**
  - It built leadworks `ready` (6 MCP tools, 4 harnesses, probe ok) and waypoint `ready` (5 tools, 4 harnesses, probe ok). With rc's kit, both had failed.
  - `talaria-app check` of the fixture: typecheck 0 errors, where rc's kit gave 5.
  - The kit-built `server.js`, imported natively under node as the host does in production, reported one zod.
- **Cleanup:** the fixtures and the leadworks install were uninstalled through `DELETE /api/admin/apps` with `wipeData`. Their app databases are gone.

**Not verified:**

- A production container image or a real instance upgrade. The upgrade was simulated by changing the host build id on the branch's own production build.
- macOS or Windows hosts.
- The host's own app-test mode (`TALARIA_APP_TESTS`). A zod-importing app test already passes there on rc, so `vitest.config.ts` is unchanged.

## Upgrade notes

- No migration, no setting and no config change.
- **From main:** the deploy changes the host build id, so the boot sweep rebuilds every installed app. An app that imports zod builds `ready` and stays enabled, as it did on main.
- **An instance that already booted rc** (staging, or any rc deploy before this PR) turned such an app off. The audit log shows `app.disable` by `system:app-health` with the zod sentence. This fix rebuilds it `ready` at the next boot but does not turn it back on. An admin re-enables it in Manage → Apps.
- **The SDK kit:** each host serves its own kit (`GET /api/sdk/kit.tgz`). A kit downloaded from an rc host before this PR still refuses zod in `talaria-app build` and `check`. Download a fresh one after the upgrade.

## Rollback

- Revert this PR. It adds no schema and no stored format.
- A reverted host has a new build id, so the boot sweep rebuilds every app. No build that links `rt-zod.js` is loaded by a host that lacks the file.
- But B3 comes back: any app that imports zod fails its build again and is turned off. Before rolling back an instance that runs leadworks or waypoint, change their `import { z } from 'zod'` to `import { z } from '@talaria/sdk/server'`, or accept that they go off.

## Branch flow

No.

## CHANGELOG entry

See `changelog/2026-11-02-apps-import-zod.md`.

entries.title: release: omapak's token check asks git whether it may push, not the account's role
entries.body:
Not ready to merge until review.

## Why

desktop-v0.12.0's Omapak submission failed at the push with a 403, after the token pre-check had passed. The pre-check read `.permissions.push` from `gh api repos/outcrop-labs/omapak`. That field is the **account's** role on the repo, not what a fine-grained token was granted, so it can't catch a token missing Contents write.

## What changed

- **`omapak-submit.yml`.** The pre-check now makes the push's own first request: receive-pack's ref advertisement (`/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`) with the token. GitHub answers:
  - 200 when the token may push;
  - 403 when it's valid but may not;
  - 401 when it's expired or unknown.
- **Error message.** It now says which of those it was, and still says what to regenerate.
- **Rejected tokens.** The account name now reads `?` instead of gh's JSON error body, which it printed to stdout before.
- **`RELEASING.md`.** One paragraph on the check.

## Verified

- **The probe's answers, using my own token:**
  - 200 for `outcrop-labs/talaria` and `outcrop-labs/omapak`, where I can push;
  - 403 for `nousresearch/hermes-agent`, which is public but I can't push to;
  - 401 for an invalid token and for no token.
- **The step's own script, pulled out of the YAML and run in bash:**
  - a valid token passes (`token for … may push`);
  - an invalid token fails with exit 1, `account: ?` and the "does not accept it" reason;
  - an empty token fails at the existing "is not set" check.
- `bun run gate` passed.

## Not verified

- **The current `OMAPAK_SUBMIT_TOKEN` itself.** I can't read the secret. Once this merges, dispatching the workflow with `desktop-v0.12.0` would show the real token failing at the pre-check (403) until it's regenerated.

entries.title: conversations: the sweep reads holds after rows — a held reply is never its orphan
entries.body:
**Not ready to merge until review.**

Fixes the flaky live test `orphan_live::lease::a_reply_this_process_writes_is_never_its_orphan`, for 0.13.2. **This is a product bug, not just a test bug.** The flake was a real race in `sweep_orphaned_replies`. The fix is in the product. The test is unchanged, and a new test pins the race.

## The failure

Both CI failures are the same assertion: [rc d9023155, run 42044630414](https://github.com/outcrop-labs/talaria/actions/runs/42044630414) and [#712 attempt 1, run 42086782220](https://github.com/outcrop-labs/talaria/actions/runs/42086782220).

```
panicked at crates/talaria-conversations/src/orphan_live.rs:196:9:
  left: None
 right: Some("124aa2dd-…")      # #712: Some("b806cc3c-…")
```

## Root cause

- `active_streaming_assistant` answers `Some(id)` for any `streaming` row this process holds (`lib.rs:1485`, `:1495`). So `None` at line 196 means the held row was no longer `streaming`.
- The conversation belongs to this test alone. In this binary, the only code that changes another test's row is a sibling test's `sweep_orphaned_replies` (`orphan_live.rs:240`, `:377`). CI's live-tests job runs no api, so nothing else touches that database.
- `sweep_orphaned_replies` read this process's holds while it built its statement (`.bind(replies_written_here())`, `lib.rs:1407` on rc). Postgres read the rows only when the statement ran.
- The test holds a fresh reply and then back-dates it 20 minutes (`held_reply`, `orphan_live.rs:173-184`). A sibling's sweep that took its hold list before that hold, and whose statement ran after the back-date, saw a row that was quiet and in neither list. It closed the row as an orphan (`error`) while its writer still held it.
- `reply_fate` and `active_streaming_assistant` already read in the safe order: the row first, then `written_here`, then the guarded close. Only the sweep read the holds first.

In production a reply is held as soon as it is inserted or resurrected, while `streamed_at = now()`. So the window needs a sweep to stall between its two reads for most of the 120 s lease. That is unlikely, but it is the same invariant the test exists to guard: "a reply this process holds … the sweep never takes it".

## The fix

`sweep_orphaned_replies` now reads the quiet `streaming` rows first, at the ordinary lease. It then drops the ones `written_here` names, and closes the rest with the unchanged guarded close (`close_orphan_sql!`, `and id = any($5::uuid[])`). In that statement the longer lease for unwritten rows still applies. A `const` assert pins `WRITER_LEASE_UNWRITTEN >= WRITER_LEASE`, which this read and `reply_fate` both rely on. With no quiet rows, the sweep is still one statement per beat.

New live test `a_sweep_under_way_when_a_reply_is_held_leaves_it_alone` forces the interleaving with no timing:
- the sweep runs on a one-connection pool whose connection is checked out;
- it is polled once, so it starts and then waits;
- the reply is held and back-dated;
- the connection is released.

## Verified

Setup: a fresh worktree off rc d3aedf96, its Postgres migrated the way CI does it (`check-migrations.ts`, 558 applied, the schema matches the snapshot). Each run is one process at a time, with `DATABASE_URL` pointed at that Postgres. The test binary was built with `cargo test -p talaria-conversations --lib`.

| schedule | before (rc) | after |
|---|---|---|
| crate's ignored tests, `--test-threads=4` (CI's runner) | **8 / 300 failed** (7 at `:196` `left: None`, 1 at `:202`) | 0 / 300, and 0 / 500 on the pushed commit |
| `orphan_live`, 4 threads | **50 / 500 failed** (all `:250`, the sweep test's own held row → `error`) | 0 / 500 |
| `orphan_live`, 8 threads | **37 / 300 failed** (1 at `:196`, 36 at `:250`) | 0 / 300 |
| `orphan_live`, 8 threads, `taskset -c 0,1` | **44 / 300 failed** | 0 / 1000 |
| `orphan_live`, default threads (48) | **33 / 300 failed** | 0 / 1000 |
| new test alone | **20 / 20 failed** (`:264`, the old sweep returned the held row) | 0 / 50 |

The new test was run against the old `lib.rs` before the fix went back in, which is how it failed 20 of 20.

Gates:
- `bun run gate` passes: `check`, plus only the `talaria-conversations` package.
- `cargo fmt -p talaria-conversations -- --check` and `cargo clippy -p talaria-conversations --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

Not run: a booted api. `keep_replies` is the sweep's only production caller (`chat-persist/src/lib.rs:1885`), and it is unchanged.

Changelog: `changelog/2026-11-09-orphan-sweep-reads-holds-after-rows.md`.

entries.title: storage: the s3 signature's date is whole seconds — backblaze refused every request
entries.body: ## What broke Connecting a Backblaze B2 bucket for replica sync failed on the first upload: ``` storage PUT 400: InvalidRequestTimestamp '20261103T173649.020Z' is invalid, must be in ISO 8601 format yyyyMMddThhmmssZ ``` `amz_of` (talaria-storage) wrote SigV4's `x-amz-date` with milliseconds. The built-in bucket accepted that, but strict S3 services (Backblaze B2, AWS) refuse it. The bug is on main as well, so any instance whose storage target or replica is a strict S3 provider fails today. ## The fix `amz_of` now writes `yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ`, dropping the milliseconds rather than rounding into the next second, so the header and the signature's scope name the same instant. Every signed request used it: the object PUT, `ensure_bucket`'s bucket PUT, the GET and the DELETE. ## Verified - The date tests are updated to SigV4's format. They cover the epoch, a leap day, and the reported instant (`1_793_727_409_020` → `20261103T173649Z`), plus `…999` ms → the same second. - AWS's documented SigV4 GET example is already pinned (`signed_get` at `20130524T000000Z`) and is unchanged, so the signing itself was right; only the date format was wrong. - `bun run check` passes. `cargo test -p talaria-storage --lib` is running locally, and CI runs the full api job. ## Not verified A live request against Backblaze B2: no account is available here. entries.title: cli: a worktree seeds its rust cache by reflink — cleanup drops a finished one's first
entries.body:
## Why

Every `bun talaria worktree` started with an empty `api/target` and paid a cold build. Each wrote its own full copy of the same third-party artifacts. On the dev host today four agent worktrees held 15, 15, 91 and 107 GiB of target, beside the primary's 34 GiB, and the disk reached the stop gate's 85% line. sccache saves the CPU, not the disk: a cache hit still writes the whole artifact into the new target.

## The design, and the options weighed

**(A) Reflink-seed at creation: chosen.** `talaria worktree` (and the new `talaria seed-target`) reflink-copies **only the registry and git units** out of the best idle checkout's `target/debug`. That is the checkout whose `Cargo.lock` shares the most `name version source` entries, most recently built first. It copies the `.fingerprint/<pkg>-<hash>` dirs, the `build/<pkg>-<hash>` dirs, and the `deps/` files whose hash is a kept unit's. Nothing of a path package (a workspace crate) is copied: no fingerprint, rlib, test binary, `incremental/`, or uplifted file. Every workspace crate compiles from the new tree's own sources.

**Why a whole copy is wrong** (the `copied-cargo-target-is-stale` trap, now explained):
- A path package's unit hash (`-C metadata`, the `-<hash>` in every file name) is computed from its path **relative to the workspace root**. So `talaria-boards` in worktree A and in worktree B look for the same artifact names.
- A path package is fresh while no source in its dep-info is newer than the dep-info file. `cp -r` stamps every file with the copy time, which is later than the new checkout's sources, so every workspace crate reads as fresh. It also scrambles the registry units' mtime order, so cargo rebuilt 118 registry crates anyway before I stopped that run. `cp -a` keeps the order, but it only narrows the race: any source build that started after the new checkout was written wins. Reproduced below on the real api.
- Registry units are safe to share. Their fingerprint is version, features and flags (`~/.cargo/registry` is immutable), so cargo judges a copied one exactly as in its own tree. Cargo itself rewrites a build script's absolute `OUT_DIR` lines (`root-output`), which exists so that a target can move.

**Safety rules in the seed:**
- It never reads a target a cargo is building in. cargo 1.97 takes `.cargo-build-lock` and `.cargo-artifact-lock` exclusively and `.cargo-lock` shared (seen in `/proc/locks` during a build). The seed checks `/proc/locks` first, which takes no lock, then copies under `flock --shared --nonblock` on all three. A build already running makes it stand down (exit 75). One that starts mid-copy waits.
- It is `cp --reflink=always` or nothing. ext4, tmpfs, or a source on another filesystem gets a cold build: never a byte copy, and never a hard link, which would share one mutable file between trees.
- It never overwrites an existing target. Any failure removes the half-made target.

**(B) A shared target dir (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or one per crate group): rejected, with evidence.**
- *Wrong:* two copies of a scratch workspace on one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Copy B's source says `ANSWER = 2` and its sources were older than A's build. `cargo run` in B printed `ANSWER=1` with no `Compiling` line: it ran A's binary. Same unit hashes, same mtime rule.
- *Serialising:* a second cargo (even `cargo check`) on that target dir printed `Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory` and waited out the first one's whole build (5.1 s for a 6 s build script). With many agents building at once, one lock means one build at a time.

**(C) Lifecycle: built into the sweep.**
- `bun talaria cleanup` now lists the build dirs of **every** linked checkout. Before, it saw only `wt/<name>` pairs, and agents rename the branch before pushing, so the 91 and 107 GiB targets were invisible to it. A renamed agent worktree is known by the `TALARIA_WORKTREE` marker in its `ui/.env`. Any other checkout's cache is reported and never removed.
- A PR that **merged or closed at the checkout's HEAD** (one batched `gh pr list`) makes the cache removable by `--apply`. Targets go before checkouts.
- A **`.talaria-keep`** is absolute: its cache is never dropped, even over the line. The report lists it as flagged for a human.
- An **open PR or no PR** keeps the cache, until the disk is **over the line**. Then `--apply` drops idle caches of clean, pushed trees: unseeded ones first, then least recently used. It drops at most **3 per run**, re-reading `statfs` after each, and stops once the disk is under the line or a drop frees **under 512 MiB** (then the pressure is not build caches). It reports what it dropped, why it stopped, and what is left.
- **Removal is rename-then-delete.** The locks are checked, the target is renamed to a sibling `.target-dropping-<pid>`, checked again, then deleted. A cargo that raced the rename still holds the moved lock's inode, so the second check sees it and the dir goes back. A leftover from an interrupted run is swept by the next `--apply`.
- **Never removed:** a cache with a cargo lock held; one built in within the last hour; one whose stack runs; the primary's; the current checkout's. A dirty or unpushed tree's cache is flagged. The older path that removes a merged worktree's checkout now makes the same lock check on its build dirs first.
- **btrfs, or no `/proc/locks`:** the lock check cannot be trusted (on btrfs, `stat`'s device is not the one `/proc/locks` prints), so nothing is deleted there. A cache that would have gone is flagged instead.
- The stop gate removes no cache, makes no extra `gh` call, and does not size the foreign targets.

**Devboxes: not seeded, on purpose.** A box builds inside its container, with the image's own rustup toolchain and a `CARGO_HOME` in its home volume. A host-built target names registry sources under the host's `~/.cargo`, from a different toolchain install. Cargo would rebuild the mismatches, so a seed would not be wrong, but its saving is unmeasured. That is a follow-up once it has been measured in a box (`docs/WORKTREES.md` says so).

## Measurements (dev host: a QEMU VM on XFS with `reflink=1`; IO pressure ran 45–90% throughout)

Build: `cargo test -p talaria-boards --no-run` (245 units: 224 registry/git units, 21 workspace crates), rc `cdaf59e7`.

| | units compiled | registry units compiled | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold worktree (sccache warm), run 1 | 245 | 224 | 15 min 01 s (includes an unknown wait on the shared package-cache lock) |
| cold worktree (sccache warm), run 2 | 245 | 224 | 25 min 34 s (again behind the package-cache lock for part of it) |
| seeded worktree, run 1 | 21 | **0** | **43 s** |
| seeded worktree, run 2 (disk stalling) | 21 | **0** | 4 min 17 s |
| seeded worktree, run 3 (right after cold run 2) | 21 | **0** | **20 s** (seed: 0.3 s) |

Disk, measured with `filefrag -v` (extents flagged `shared`), because `du` counts reflinked bytes twice:

| target | `du` | unique extents | shared extents |
|---|---|---|---|
| a cold worktree's (run 2) | 1.4 GiB | **1522 MiB** | 3 MiB |
| a seeded worktree's, after its build (both seeded trees) | 1.4 GiB | **415 MiB** | 1111 MiB |

The seed itself took 0.3 s (14.7 s during a stall) for 314 registry units in 2664 files. `df` moved by less than its noise (−2 MiB). So this build's cache costs 415 MiB of new disk per worktree instead of 1522 MiB (−73%). The remainder is the workspace crates, which must be compiled here. For the full workspace (244 path crates) the share that seeding saves is smaller, since most of a big target is workspace test binaries. The lifecycle rules above are what reclaim those.

## The correctness proof

Two throwaway rc worktrees were cut **before** the source worktree built, so every source file in them is older than every fingerprint in the source target. That is the exact condition the trap needs. In each, `role_rank("owner")` changed from 3 to 7 and a test `seed_proof_owner_ranks_seven` asserting 7 was added, with the file's mtime set back to its checkout time.

- **Whole copy** (`cp -a --reflink=always` of the source target, sources stamped at their checkout time): `cargo test -p talaria-boards --lib` compiled **0** units, ran **6** tests, and printed `test result: ok`. The new test was not in the binary: rc's code ran and passed in a tree whose source says otherwise.
- **Same tree, seeded** (`rm -rf api/target`, `talaria seed-target --from ../talaria-seedcold`): it compiled 21 units, all workspace crates and **no registry crate**, then ran **7** tests, including `seed_proof_owner_ranks_seven ... ok`.
- The other worktree, seeded the same way: the same 21 units and 7 tests.

## Verified
- The real api, as above: `cargo test -p talaria-boards` in cold, seeded, and whole-copied rc worktrees on this host. I ran no workspace cargo.
- The scratch workspace: the whole-copy trap (`ANSWER=1`), the seed (`ANSWER=2`, `itoa` not recompiled), the shared-target-dir stale run and its lock wait, and the no-reflink fallback on tmpfs (`cannot reflink … a cold build`).
- `cli` `bun test`: 482 pass (a destination that cannot be made is a failed seed, not a throw). `targetseed.test.ts` covers the selection (never a workspace crate, or a name that is both, or an unvouched file), `/proc/locks` parsing, the flock and `cp` argv, the fallbacks, and a real run. That real run took the reflink path on XFS (`TMPDIR` on `/home`) and the fallback on tmpfs. `worktree.test.ts` covers `--seed-from`, `--no-seed`, no reflink with the stack still whole, and the contradicting flags. `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `scripts/cleanup-sweep.test.mjs` (76 checks; the rename and re-check, and the merged-worktree refusal, run against a real `flock -x` holder, on tmpfs and on XFS). Also covered: finished-PR, dirty, busy, hot and running-stack cases, foreign checkouts, LRU order under pressure, no double count, targets first, and `prStateAt`. A dry `inventory()` on this host (no removal) found the targets of renamed agent worktrees for the first time. It would remove one cache, `talaria-work-view`'s (PR merged, idle, stack down), and keeps every live one: open PR, `.talaria-keep`, a cargo building, or a running stack. `talaria-jev` (merged) and `talaria-coding-accounts` (33 days idle) stay while their stacks run.
- `bun run check`, `bun run gate`, `scripts/judge-pr.mjs` (0 must, 0 should; the one ask is the regenerated `docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md`, which gains `talaria seed-target` and the three `worktree` flags).

## Not verified
- Every `--apply` removal on this host. I ran no `--apply` here: other sessions' worktrees are live. The removal paths are tested with planted rows only.
- The pressure-drop loop against a real full disk. Its bounds (cap, freed-too-little stop, back under the line, a failed drop) are tested with an injected disk reading.
- btrfs itself. The detection is `statfs` `f_type == 0x9123683E`, tested by injection; this host is XFS.
- `talaria worktree` end to end with its stack. I seeded by `seed-target`, the same function the worktree step calls. The worktree path is covered by `worktree.test.ts`, because main's database seed raced at creation on this host earlier today, which is unrelated.
- The `--desktop` target, seeded by the same code with a different cargo root.
- macOS, which has no `/proc/locks` and no `flock` (the seed says so and builds cold), and a devbox.
- A clean cold-build time: the first cold run waited behind the shared package-cache lock for an unknown share of its 15 minutes, and the disk stalled throughout.

entries.title: ui: chat groups a sender's run into one block — avatar, name and time once, like Slack
entries.body:
# Pull request

**Base branch: `rc`.** This is for v0.13.1.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR targets `rc`.
- [x] `bun run gate` is green locally.
- [x] I exercised the changed path in the running app. The steps are under **Verified**.
- [x] A `changelog/2026-11-04-chat-message-grouping.md` file says what changed and what was verified.
- [x] Generated files: none touched.

## What changed

Chat now groups consecutive messages from one sender, as Slack does. The first message of a run shows the avatar, the name and the time. Later messages render as continuation lines. Hovering or focusing one shows its own time in the avatar column. This is presentation only: there is no API or storage change.

**Where messages render.** There are two row families and three lists, and all of them now call one pure function, `ui/src/lib/message-groups.ts`:
- `ChannelView` with `MessageRow` renders Comms channels, 1:1 and group DMs, and ticket discussions (TaskDetail mounts ChannelView).
- `ThreadPanel` with `MessageRow` (`inThread`) renders threads.
- `ChatView` with `UserTurn` and `AssistantTurn` renders agent DMs and WorkHarness work, research and plan sessions.

`InboxChatPanel` (the inbox assistant panel) is not changed. It renders bubbles with no avatar, name or time header, so there is nothing to merge.

**The grouping rules** are in the module comment. A row starts a new block when:
- the sender changes;
- more than `GROUP_GAP_MS` passes since the previous message. The threshold is **5 minutes**, measured between consecutive messages. The comparison is strict, so a gap of exactly 5:00 still groups;
- the row is stamped **before** the previous one. It groups only when `0 <= d <= GROUP_GAP_MS`. A row the client drew on a slow clock therefore cannot join and then split when the sync swaps in the server's time;
- the row opens a new day (the list's own day-divider map is passed in, so the two always agree);
- either row has no parseable time. `DisplayMessage.createdAt` is optional, so the type allows this;
- the caller marks the row `fresh`. This covers an agent's scheduled-run turn (`cronJobId`, because the agent spoke up unprompted and the time matters) and the first reply under a thread root. The root stands alone above the "N replies" rule.

Each surface maps its rows to these inputs in a pure, tested helper:
- `channelGroupFacts` and `threadGroupFacts` in the new `components/chat/channel-groups.ts`, which has type-only imports;
- `turnGroupFacts` in `chat-view.ts`.

The `.svelte` files only pass that helper to `messageBlocks`.

Status, content, tools, reactions and replies never affect grouping. A streaming message is grouped exactly as it will be once it settles, so arriving tokens never move a header. An agent's tool-only turn stays in its run, and its tool disclosure says what it is. A deleted message leaves the list, and the rows around it regroup.

**Accessibility.** Every row now renders a `<time datetime>` (`MessageTime.svelte`) with the full date and time as its `title`. A continuation line's visible short label ("3:05") is `aria-hidden`. A screen reader hears sr-only text in the header's format instead ("03:05 PM"), because `title` is not reliably announced on an element nothing focuses. On a continuation line, the time is hidden with opacity, not `display`. That keeps it in the accessibility tree, next to a visually hidden author name (`sr-only`, the Tailwind utility the repo already uses), so a screen reader hears who sent each line and when. The repo has no tooltip primitive for a bare element (InfoTip is an icon button), so this follows the chat rows' existing native-`title` pattern.

**Layout.** Each list cancels its own `space-y` gap for `[data-continued]` rows. MessageActions, ReactionChips, the thread rollup, attachments, ChatChips, GuardCaveat, the streaming caret, ChatWaiting and the error lines are all unchanged inside a continuation line. A continuation line has no header, so its `(edited)` mark sits after the body. The header time format is unchanged. The gutter time drops the day period ("1:06", not "01:06 PM") so it fits the 24 px avatar column, and the title carries the full stamp. `docs/UI-CONVENTIONS.md` gains one bullet saying that grouping lives in this one function.

There are no unread dividers in any chat surface to regress; only read cursors exist.

## Verified

- **Gate:** `bun run gate` passed: `check` clean, svelte-check reported 0 errors and 0 warnings, and vitest ran 203 files with 3092 tests passing. `node scripts/judge-pr.mjs --base origin/rc` reported 0 must, 0 should and 0 ask.
- **Unit:** `ui/src/lib/message-groups.test.ts` covers the rules:
  - the threshold pinned at exactly `5 * 60 * 1000`;
  - the same sender inside the threshold;
  - the gap measured between consecutive messages;
  - a sender change;
  - a user next to an agent;
  - a gap of exactly the threshold, and one 1 ms over;
  - a negative gap, and the clock-skew pair before and after the sync;
  - a day boundary at 23:58 → 00:01, through the real `dayDividerMap`;
  - a deleted message, including a deleted block head;
  - a `fresh` row;
  - a missing or unparseable time;
  - epoch-ms and `Date` instants;
  - an empty list;
  - `continuationSet`.

  The surface helpers are tested through the real `messageBlocks`:
  - `channel-groups.test.ts`: grouping by author; the author type in the key; status ignored (streaming, growing, settled and errored); the thread root standing alone; later replies grouping.
  - `chat-view.test.ts`: a scheduled run starts fresh, and the same turn without the marker continues; a client-drawn row with no `authorUserId` joins the viewer's run; two `authorUserId`s on a shared plan; a user and the agent kept apart; status, content and tools ignored from first token to settled. It also adds 4 cases for `gutterTime`, `fullTime` and `isoTime`.
- **Mutation check:** each of these 7 deliberate breaks fails exactly one test:
  - the thread rule changed to `i === 0`;
  - `fresh: !!m.cronJobId` dropped;
  - `turnGroupFacts` reading status;
  - `channelGroupFacts` reading status;
  - a negative gap grouping;
  - a 10-minute threshold;
  - no viewer fallback.
- **Exercised:** in headless Chromium (Playwright), against this branch's fresh worktree stack: app :5309, api :5409, its own Postgres and Redis, with no push or mail configured. The seed had a channel with runs from Ada, Ben and the agent Scout, including one run from yesterday and a 10-minute same-sender gap. It also had a DM with a 21-minute gap, and an agent conversation with a user run, an agent run containing a tool-only turn, an 8-minute gap and an errored turn. Results:
  - Channel: 14 rows formed 7 headers and 7 continuations, exactly as the rules predict. The 10-minute Ben gap split the run, and the 1-minute follow-up joined it.
  - DM: 7 rows formed 3 headers and 4 continuations.
  - Agent chat: the user run and the agent run each grouped, the tool-only turn stayed in the agent's block, and the gap and the error each started a new block.
  - Hovering a continuation line took its gutter `<time>` to opacity 1, with the title "Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at 12:34 PM".
  - Reactions: a 🙌 added from the hover toolbar on a continuation line showed as a chip.
  - Threads: "3 replies" opened from a block. In the panel the root stood alone and Ada's two replies grouped.
  - Edit: a live edit of a continuation line saved, stayed a continuation, and showed `(edited)`.
  - The attachment chip rendered inside a block.
  - Sends: two live sends in a row. The first started a new block because it came more than 5 minutes after the previous message. The second joined it.
  - Delete: deleting a block's first message moved the header to the next line.
  - The `· interrupted` failed state rendered inside a block.
  - Themes: Mercury and Mercury Light at 1280 px and 760 px, with no horizontal scroll and no page errors.
  - Playwright's `ariaSnapshot()` of each transcript lists a `time` and the author for every line.
  - **After the review fixes,** a re-run on a fresh stack checked the screen-reader times. In the channel (14 lines, 7 continuations), the DM (7 lines, 4) and the agent chat (8 lines, 3), every `time` in the accessibility snapshot carries AM/PM (for example "01:24 PM"), while the visible gutter label stays short ("1:24"). There were no page errors.

  Screenshots, the aria snapshots, `report.json` and the seed and exercise scripts are saved in the session's `release/chat-grouping/` evidence directory.

## Not verified

- **Mobile:** web only. The native mobile app's `MessageRow` (`CommsScreen.kt`) still shows a header on every row; the changelog says so.

- Ticket discussions and the WorkHarness work, research and plan panes were not opened in the browser. They mount the same `ChannelView` and `ChatView` that were exercised.
- The agent chat was exercised with a stopped stand-in agent and seeded turns. A live streaming turn was not run, because this stack has no model provider. A streaming row's grouping is covered by the unit case: the grouping inputs (sender and time) do not change while it streams.
- Emoji glyphs show as boxes in the screenshots because headless Chromium on this host has no emoji font. The chips' text and counts were read from the DOM.
- At 390 px the Comms sidebar does not collapse and crushes the transcript. That layout is unchanged by this PR. The narrow check used 760 px and the thread panel, which is about 360 px wide.
- No real screen reader was used. The accessibility tree was read through Playwright.

## Branch flow

No.

## Review findings

- Fixed: 1 (per-surface wiring tests), 2 (spoken AM/PM), 3 (negative gap), 4 (unreachable rules dropped) and 7 (threshold pinned).
- 8: the changelog now says the change is web only.
- 5 and 6 are left as they are, as agreed.

## CHANGELOG entry

See `changelog/2026-11-04-chat-message-grouping.md`.

entries.title: work: a live ticket says what its agent is doing — step, clock, output, cost, failures
entries.body:
## What was wrong (outcrop, 2026-11-04, read-only)

| Defect | Evidence |
|---|---|
| One phase for a working session and a waiting one | All three sessions sat on `turn 1 of 12 — waiting on doug-engineering` for 40+ minutes while running builds. Later two sat on `turn 2 …` for 70+ minutes while looping on `process_manage wait`. |
| The ticket strip printed the turn twice | `Doug is working this ticket · turn 1 · turn 1 of 12 — waiting on doug-engineering` |
| No current step, elapsed time or last output outside the watch modal | TALA-93's `cargo test -p talaria-notify` and TALA-92's 420 s build kill were in the watch tail only, and its frames carried no times. |
| No sign of a turn sent but not taken (agent booting, at its run cap, unreachable) | `runs.agent_run_id` holds this; nothing read it. |
| Queue position without "behind what" | |
| No tokens or cost per ticket, and no reason | 926 calls, none on a ticket: they were on the shared fleet key, and Hermes v0.21 does not send the session header. |
| Failures hidden | A failed log row was a red chip without its reason. Tool failures during a live turn were invisible. A refused workbench tool frame did not say it failed. |
| Provisioning failures had nowhere to render | |

## Change

- **`talaria-work-pulse` (new crate).** Every watch-tail writer stamps its frame with `at`: stream frames in the harness transport, plugin frames in `tool_events`, and workbench `wtool` frames, which now also carry `ok`. Each turn records when it began (`run-watch:<id>:turn`). A bounded read of the tail's last 128 KB gives the running step and its parent, the last finished step, the last output, the agent's last sentence, and recent failures. One call that both the stream and the plugin report, in either order, counts as one step.
- **`talaria-routes-boards` `work_status`.** `GET /api/tasks/{id}/work-session` and `GET /api/boards/{id}/work-sessions` carry `activity`, `spend`, `startedAt` and the server's `now`.
  - `activity.state` comes from the run row first. A queued run reads `queued`, with no dead step from before a restart. An awaiting run reads `awaiting`. Otherwise it is running, thinking, quiet, or `sending`, where the agent has not taken the turn. A pulse Redis could not read is `unknown`.
  - `spend` holds tokens and cost from the gateway's priced view. A partly priced total shows its unpriced count. When nothing is on the ticket, `missing` gives a reason only when it is this agent's in this session's window: `untagged`, meaning its own calls carried no session key (crons excluded), or `shared-key`, meaning it worked, nothing landed under its own name, and shared-key calls arrived.
  - A queued ticket's `behind` names only tickets on boards the reader has a role on. `behindHidden` counts the rest.
  - History rows carry `error`.
  - The pulse is cached per run by tail length and turn marker, and served again within 2 s, so board polls re-read only changed tails.
- **UI.** `WorkPulse` sits on the ticket strip, and in two lines on kanban cards and list rows. Clocks tick from one shared timer against the server's clock. The duplicated turn is gone. Work-log rows show why a session ended. Job rows render #706's `provision` (state, step, error, output) when the job read carries it. All of it uses `ui/` primitives (`Chip`).

No status or column writes, and no migration.

## Verified
- `cargo test` passes for `talaria-work-pulse` (9), `talaria-work-wait` (6) and `talaria-routes-boards` (3). They cover:
  - the tail reader's outcrop shapes, parallel calls, plugin-first pairing, and a command mentioning `"at":`;
  - the cache rule;
  - the state word against queued, re-queued and awaiting runs;
  - each attribution reason and when it stays silent;
  - the behind split.
- New live test `work_wait_behind_live`, run by CI's api-integration: one agent with sessions on two boards that have different members, and each reader sees only their own board's ticket by name.
- `work-pulse.test.ts`, including partial pricing and the behind line, passes. `svelte-check` reports 0 errors.
- First version, on a `workobs` worktree stack with a real Hermes v0.22.4 Developer Agent and a mock upstream, with three then six live tickets:
  - The board showed each `running` with its own shell step and clock, and tokens booked per ticket.
  - It showed `quiet` with its age while the agent was slow.
  - A failed turn's error appeared in the Work log.
- `bun run gate` passes.

## Not verified
- The `shared-key` and `untagged` reasons against a real v0.21 agent. They are tested as pure logic over ledger counts shaped like outcrop's.
- The revised state words and the cache on a running stack. The proof stack from the first version was torn down; this round is unit, live-DB and CI.
- `provision` rendering until #706 merges. It matches #706's `Record::to_json` field names.

entries.title: tasks: assigning a ticket never moves it or starts work — and a person's move lifts Stop
entries.body:
**Not ready to merge until review.** This replaces #704 with the narrow fix the owner asked for: "all i wanted was the board to stop letting agent tickets start as soon as they were assigned."

## What changes

1. **Assigning never moves a ticket.** `update_task` no longer moves an intake ticket into the agent column because someone was assigned (the "(promoted by assignment)" move). The ticket stays in its column.
2. **Creating never moves a ticket either.** `create_task` puts a new ticket where its creator chose, and in intake by default. Its assignees never pick the column.
   - The create route takes an optional `status` from a person. Agents' tickets still land in intake, and an agent naming a column gets a 403.
   - The Kanban "add card" flow is unchanged: it still creates the ticket, then moves it.
3. **Assignment starts work only in a pickup column.** `maybe_dispatch_ticket` already dispatches only from pickup columns, so with the promotion gone, assigning an agent elsewhere starts nothing. These still start work, as on rc:
   - assigning an agent to a ticket already in a pickup column;
   - a person moving a ticket into a pickup column;
   - creating a ticket in a pickup column by choice.
4. **A person's Stop lifts again.** `dispatch_block` lifted only on a status line whose actor was a user id. The board records a person's moves under their email, so a Stop never lifted. It now lifts on a move whose actor names a user by email or id.

**Unchanged from rc:**
- work sessions move their own ticket (In progress, Quality review, Blocked);
- `report_outcome` and the prompts and brief text;
- `triage_ticket` and `move_ticket` (no approval cards);
- plugin change requests and plugin upkeep tickets: still born in the board's pickup column (rc's `assigned_key`), and they still start the maintainer (see the caller table below);
- plugin PR upkeep, the sweep, and the review queues.

There is no migration. Tickets that an earlier assignment already moved into agent columns stay there; a person can move them back.

**Diff:**
- `talaria-tasks`: promotion removed from `update_task`; `create_task` gains `NewTask.status`.
- `talaria-routes-boards`: optional `status` on POST `/api/boards/{id}/tasks`, with `docs/api/boards.md` regenerated.
- `talaria-work-dispatch`: the Stop lift now matches by email or user id, plus three live tests.
- `talaria-tasks`: `pickup_column(pg, board_id)`, the board's `assigned_key`, for internal callers whose ticket is an ask for the agent's work.
- `talaria-plugins`: a change request and an upkeep ticket with a maintainer are created with `status` set to `pickup_column`, so they keep rc's column and dispatch. The helpdesk problem report passes `status: None`.
- `docs/APPS.md`: one row.
- UI type: `createTask` accepts `status`.
- A changelog entry.

## Every internal `create_task` caller

Only board and MCP creation by people and agents changes. MCP's `create_ticket` posts to the same board route.

| Caller | Assignees | rc: column, started? | Now: column, started? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/boards/{id}/tasks` (board UI, MCP, agents) | any | assigned → `assigned_key`, started | creator's chosen column (people only), else intake; starts only if chosen column is a pickup column |
| `talaria-plugins` `change::request_change` (Manage → Apps change request) | the maintainer | `assigned_key`, started | `assigned_key` (named by the caller), started |
| `talaria-plugins` `upkeep` (upkeep ticket) | the maintainer, if any | with one: `assigned_key`, started; without: intake, not started | the same |
| `talaria-routes-fleet` `agent_problem` (helpdesk problem report) | none | intake, not started | intake, not started |

All other ticket inserts in the api are test fixtures. A board without a usable agent column has no `assigned_key`. There the plugin tickets land in intake, as rc's `.or_else(default_key)` did.

## Verified

- **`bun run gate`** (on `84c5dc31`): check, ui svelte-check and 3136 tests, and fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for talaria-api, -plugins, -routes-boards, -routes-fleet, -tasks and -work-dispatch.
- **New live-DB tests in `talaria-work-dispatch` `live_db`** (4 of 4 pass, counting the existing sweep test). They use the real push (the boot seam wired) and the real dispatch assembly:
  - `assignment_on_create_or_update_never_moves_a_ticket_or_starts_work`: a ticket created assigned stays in Inbox with no session. A ticket assigned afterwards stays in Inbox, with no move line and no session, and the sweep's gate starts nothing.
  - `assignment_starts_work_only_in_a_pickup_column`: each of these starts a session:
    - a person moving the ticket into Assigned;
    - assigning an agent to a ticket already in Assigned;
    - creating a ticket in Assigned by choice.
  - `a_persons_move_lifts_their_stop_whether_it_names_their_email_or_id`.
- **With rc's behaviour restored** (the promotion on update and create, and the user-id-only Stop check):
  - the first test fails: an assignee chose the column, giving `assigned`, not `inbox`;
  - the third fails: the Stop did not lift after an email-recorded move.
  - The second covers behaviour rc already has; it guards that the fix keeps it.
- **New live test `talaria-api` `plugin_tickets_live`:** `request_change` with the real push and dispatch assembly. The change request's ticket lands in `assigned`, the board's pickup column, and starts a maintainer session. A ticket created with the same assignee and no column lands in `inbox` and starts nothing. On the previous head (`2045fde1`, `status: None`) the first assertion fails with `inbox`.

## Not verified

- **No end-to-end run in the app with a live agent.** The tests drive the same write paths and the real dispatch gate.

entries.head: fb6431bc08de1edad06ed7ccb25aea7f74ecc4be
entries.title: apps: grants leave with the app — another repository under its slug starts with none (FB12)
entries.body:
Release-sweep batch **FB12**. Findings fixed: **apps-1** (app grants survive uninstall and pass to a different repository under the same slug) and **apps-7** (the documented free probe ignores the harness's own model setting).

## apps-1: grants leave with the app

**Root cause.** People's and teams' grants on an app (`/x/<slug>`, `/x/<slug>/manage` in `allowed_manage_views` and `denied_views` of `users` and `teams`) are named by slug alone. `uninstall_app` removed the code, the DB container, the MCP row and its grants, but never these rows. The install path already treats another repository under the slug as another app for its *data* (409, adopt or wipe), but the grants carried straight over. A different repository installed later under the same slug, even after `keptData: "wipe"`, gave its members every surface the old app's members held. That contradicts "apps are explicit-grant: enabling one gives members nothing" (docs/APPS.md). Not a regression (main never pruned them either), but rc's own kept-data rule now calls that install a different app.

**Decision: a reinstall of the same repository keeps its grants, judged by repository identity, not slug.** The identity is the record the slug's data directory already keeps (`app-data/<slug>/source.json`: host plus the owner/name path, compared without case, which is the existing `DataSource::same_repo`).
- **Uninstall** keeps the grants with kept data (uninstall-keep is built to be reversed by reinstalling the same repository, and the record names whose they are). When it keeps no data (wipe, or the app never stored anything) it removes them and their denials, from users and teams. Nothing would be left to say whose they were.
- **Install** keeps them only when that record names the repository being installed, even when the same repository wipes its own data. Another repository starts with none whether it adopts the data or wipes it, and so does any install of a slug whose grants no record vouches for. The grants follow the repository; the data follows the choice.
- Removal is one transaction over both tables. It drops `/x/<slug>`, `/x/<slug>/manage` and any route below them, matched without case as `app_view_for` reads a path. Other apps' views (a `<slug>-two` app included), core views and list order are untouched.
- Install and uninstall answer `grantsRemoved` (how many people and teams held one), and the `app.install` / `app.uninstall` audit rows carry it. This is additive. The UI reads neither field.

**The upgrade: no migration.** The install-time rule drops any grant on a slug that no record vouches for. So a grant a pre-fix uninstall left orphaned is dropped the moment anything is installed under that slug, unless it is the same repository's kept data, which is the intended keep. Verified live below (`grantsRemoved: 3` on the first install after rc's uninstalls). A SQL migration could not do better, for two reasons:
- It cannot see which apps exist. Checkout and hand-placed apps, the owner's among them, have no `app_sources` row, so a "not installed" predicate would strip live grants.
- Grants a pre-fix install already carried over onto an app installed today look exactly like grants given since. Nothing records provenance. **Release note:** an admin who installed a different repository under a reused slug before this release should review who holds that app's views.

**Rollback safety.** No schema change, no migration, and no new setting. Rolled back, main reads the same columns; the only difference is that entries this build removed stay removed. Main's view of those entries: they belonged to an app no longer installed, or to another repository. The response and audit fields are additive.

## apps-7: the free probe uses the slot

`docs/sdk/harnesses.md` told apps to guard runs with `resolveHarnessModel(triage.model)`. The bound runner (`ctx.harness.run`) stamps `slot: app:<slug>/<harness id>` and resolves it first. The spec carries no slot, so where the admin's assignment is the only model that routes, the probe answered null and the route fell back on every call. The example, the export table, `docs/sdk/reference.md` and the apps product skill now probe with `{ ...def.model, slot: \`app:${ctx.app}/${def.id}\` }`. Docs only: the hunter's alternative, a bound `ctx.harness.resolve(def)`, is an SDK change and is left for later.

## Files beyond the expected three, and why
- `api/crates/talaria-apps/src/lifecycle/live.rs`: the live test module of `lifecycle.rs`, which holds the new test and the existing tests' adjustments to `uninstall_app`'s new return type.
- `docs/APPS.md`: it states the uninstall and explicit-grant contract that changed.
- `docs/api/admin.md`: regenerated by `bun run docs:api`; the Returns column gained `grantsRemoved`.
- `docs/sdk/reference.md`, `scripts/skills/talaria-apps/references/harnesses.md`: the same probe sentence as harnesses.md. The skill is what agents writing apps read.
- `ui/src/sdk/server.test.ts`: transcribes the doc's probe (that file's purpose) and replaces a comment that named the old expression.
- `changelog/2026-11-02-app-grants-leave-with-the-app.md`.

## Verified
- **The new test fails on the old code.** `grants_go_back_only_to_their_own_repository` (live, `#[ignore]`d like its neighbours; CI's live-tests job runs it) was run against rc's `lifecycle.rs` and failed at `another repository`: repo B's install still held all of A's grants and denials. With the fix: `cargo test -p talaria-apps --lib -- --include-ignored lifecycle::` against a migrated Postgres, 12 passed. The new test covers:
  - a member and a team with allowed and denied views, plus a case-variant denial, a `<slug>-two` app and core views;
  - kept, then reinstalled (kept);
  - another repository refused (untouched), then wiped (removed, 2);
  - explicit adopt of another repository's data (removed);
  - the same repository wiping its own data (kept);
  - an uninstall with nothing stored (removed);
  - an orphan (removed);
  - an uninstall wipe (removed), then a second sweep (0).
- Unit test `grants_belong_only_to_the_recorded_repository` (capitals, another owner, another host, no record). Vitest: the doc's probe with the slot answers `step: 'slot'`, the bare spec answers null, and the doc's slot string equals the host's `appHarnessSlot`.
- `bun run gate`: check, svelte-check 0 errors, vitest 2941 passed, and fmt/clippy/tests for `talaria-apps` and `talaria-routes-admin`.
- **Live, on a worktree stack (rc 678dd627, slot 9), with scratch repos X and Y both named `talaria-app-fb12grant` and test users only:**
  - **rc's api:** install X, grant work@ the work view, mgr@ the manage view and a team the work view, store a note, uninstall keeping the data. Installing Y is refused (409); with `keptData: "wipe"` it installs. Y's `whoami` answered **200** to work@, mgr@ and the team member, and work@'s session held `appGrants: ["/x/fb12grant"]`. A wipe uninstall of Y left every grant on the rows.
  - **The fixed api:**
    - The first install of X answered `grantsRemoved: 3`, dropping the orphans rc had left.
    - The same sequence then gave **403** to all four users and `appGrants: []`. Y's install answered `grantsRemoved: 3`, and only mgr@'s core `/apps` grant was left.
    - Uninstall keeping the data answered `grantsRemoved: 0`. A reinstall of the same repository (Y) adopted the data with its grants (200 for work@ and the team member).
    - An uninstall wipe removed them (`grantsRemoved: 2`), with the data directory gone. The audit rows carry the counts.
  - **apps-7:** a scratch app running the doc's probe verbatim answered `bare: null, slotted: {model: "Z.ai coding/glm-4.7-flash", step: "slot"}` once its slot was assigned. No model call was made.

## Not verified
- The Manage → Apps uninstall and install buttons in a browser. The API they call was exercised.
- The plugin approval path (`request_app_install`). It calls the same `install_app`.
- A GitHub or Forgejo source. The identity rule is the existing `same_repo`, unit-tested on GitHub URLs; live runs used `file://` repositories.
- The desktop and mobile surfaces are untouched.


## Review round (871a8d0f)

- **should-2: a no-data uninstall no longer drops a same-repository reinstall's grants.**
  - Short of a wipe, uninstall keeps `app-data/<slug>/source.json` even when the app stored nothing, alone in the directory, and keeps the grants with it. A repair (uninstall, then the same repository) therefore keeps who may use the app.
  - A lone record is not kept data (`has_kept_data`), so another repository installs fresh with no 409 and its install drops the grants. A wipe takes both the record and the grants.
  - For an install that predates the record, uninstall writes it from `app_sources` (`record_to_keep`).
  - Live, every app the real host builds gets its database, UI-only ones included. So this path is reached only when the app's database never started. The Rust live test covers it, with a mock host.
  - A renamed or transferred repository is another repository: adopting its data does not carry its grants. That is now documented in APPS.md and the changelog.
- **should-3: grants are removed before the app is placed (left as is: it fails closed).**
  - If the rename or `write_source` then fails, the install fails with the grants already gone, never handed over. The cost is that a later reinstall of the old repository finds its data but must be granted again.
  - Stale record, decided: an install that drops another repository's grants now also removes that repository's `source.json` before placing the app (`forget_data_source`, an error that stops the install if removal fails).
  - The write of the new record after placement stays a warning. If it fails, no record is left, so nothing vouches and the next install drops the grants. The old record can no longer survive to vouch for the new app's grants (the review's nit-2 case).
- **should-1.**
  - The changelog and APPS.md tell admins to review who holds `/x/<slug>` and `/x/<slug>/manage` on a slug already reused for another repository. That repository's own record now vouches for grants it inherited before this release, so they are not cleaned automatically.
  - Manage → Apps now shows `grantsRemoved` in the install notice (Discover tab). The uninstall prompt now says that deleting the data takes the grants, and that keeping it keeps them for a reinstall of the same repository. Plain text, no new component.
- **The harness docs' "never borrow" sentence was false, so it is now enforced.**
  - The free probe and the free `runHarness` took `model.slot` from app code as written. So an app could read, and with the free runner run on, another app's assigned model (`app:<other>/<id>`).
  - Both now keep a slot only when it is the calling app's own, judged by the host's `appInScope()` and not the app's word. Any other slot is dropped and logged once (`ownSlotOnly`, `resolveHarnessModelForApp`; the SDK still exports it as `resolveHarnessModel`).
  - Tests: own slot kept, another harness of the same app kept, `app:billing/…`, `app:<slug>-two/…` and a non-app slot dropped, no slot outside any scope, and the free runner ignoring a foreign slot. The free-runner test fails with the guard unhooked.
  - Live: the probe app answered `foreign: null` for kit-notes's assigned slot while its own slot resolved, and the host logged the drop.
- **Files added this round:** `ui/src/server/app-harness-runner.ts` and its test, `ui/src/sdk/server.ts`, `ui/src/routes/app/{AppsDiscoverTab,AppsInstalledTab}.svelte`, `ui/src/routes/app/apps.ts`.
- **Verified:**
  - `cargo test -p talaria-apps --lib -- --include-ignored lifecycle::`: 12 passed, in three full runs. One earlier full run failed once in the unchanged update test: its mock host saw two requests with no step. That did not recur in six more runs and is not in code this PR touches.
  - `bun run gate` passes: svelte-check 0 errors, vitest 2945, fmt/clippy/tests for both crates.
  - Live on the slot-9 stack: same-repository reinstall kept its grants (`grantsRemoved: 0`, 200), a wipe removed them (`grantsRemoved: 2`), and the slot guard behaved as above. Scratch apps and test users were removed afterwards, and the stack was stopped.
- **Trailer:** the commits carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5`, which is this session's model.


## Re-review round (fb6431bc)

- **should-A, a check-then-use gap in the slot guard: fixed.**
  - The gap: `ownSlotOnly` checked `spec.slot` and then handed on the app's own object, which the resolver read again. A getter or Proxy could show the app's own slot to the check and another app's slot to the chain.
  - The fix: it now reads every field once into a plain copy the host built (the chain into a fresh array) and passes only that copy on. The free runner reads `def.model` once and replaces it with the copy.
  - Tests: a getter slot, a Proxy spec (each with a reader that flips after three reads, in both orders), and the free runner. All three fail against 871a8d0f's guard.
- **`record_to_keep` hardening: done.**
  - The host's `app_sources` row now wins whenever there is one, and the file is rewritten from it (`keep_record`). The on-disk `source.json`, which a running app can write, stands alone only for an app with no row.
  - Tests: the unit test `the_host_row_wins_over_a_record_the_app_could_write` and a forged-record step in the live test. Both fail with the file preferred.
- **`forget_data_source` is pinned.**
  - A `#[cfg(test)]` switch (`FAIL_NEXT_INSTALL_RECORD`) fails the one record write an install makes after placement.
  - The live test then asserts that no stale record survives: after a lone record of A and a failed write for B, there is no record rather than A's. Removing the call fails it at exactly that assertion.
  - The unit test `forgetting_a_record_that_is_not_there_is_no_error` covers NotFound and an unremovable record.
- **harnesses.md** now says an app cannot read or run on another app's setting "through the SDK", which matches nit-A: the guard is as strong as app scope.
- **Verified:**
  - `cargo test -p talaria-apps --lib -- --include-ignored lifecycle::`: 14 passed.
  - `bun run gate` passes: svelte-check 0 errors, vitest 2948, and fmt/clippy/tests for both crates.
  - I did not start the stack for a live HTTP run this round; the changes are covered by the tests above. The database was started only for those tests and then stopped.

entries.title: release: server tags stop building desktop installers — desktop ships as desktop-v only
entries.body:
Owner decision: Talaria Desktop ships only as `desktop-vX.Y.Z` releases, minted by `desktop-package.yml` on a main push. Before this change, a `vX.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` tag also built installers stamped with the server version and attached them. A Desktop numbered 0.13.0 beside `desktop-v0.12.0` would never be offered an update until Desktop passed 0.13.

## What changed

- `release.yml`: the `desktop-package` job (the `workflow_call` into `desktop-package.yml`) is removed. Nothing listed it in `needs:`. The header and the GitHub Release comment no longer claim that every tag publish builds the desktop installers. The image, api package, CI call and GitHub Release steps are unchanged, and every `v*` release still opens `--latest=false`.
- `desktop-package.yml`: the triggers are unchanged. The `workflow_call` stays as an inert trigger with no caller. Comments that described `attach` running into release.yml's `vX.Y.Z` releases now describe the re-attach dispatch, the only non-mint path left.
- `omapak-submit.yml`: only `desktop-v*` tags move the store pin. A hand-published server `v*` release used to qualify, but it no longer carries a desktop build.
- `scripts/release-latest.mjs` and `scripts/check-invariants.mjs`: comment and message wording only. The check logic is unchanged.
- Docs: RELEASING.md (the RC paragraph, Latest, "The desktop installers", omapak), the `cut-release` skill, docs/DESKTOP.md "Installers" and the updater section, docs/BRANCHES.md, docs/MOBILE.md, DEVELOPERS.md.
- `changelog/2026-11-04-server-tags-carry-no-desktop.md`.

## Verified

- `bun run check` exits 0, including the workflow invariants. `release-latest-is-the-desktop-feed` reports "release.yml never takes it; desktop-package.yml takes it after latest.json lands, on the mint path only".
- I read the workflows to confirm nothing else depended on the removed job:
  - `release.yml` has no other reference to `desktop-package`, and none of its jobs listed it in `needs:`.
  - SHA256SUMS, `latest.json` and the Latest flip all live inside `desktop-package.yml`'s `attach`, and they still run on its own mint path.
  - The job's `contents: write` grant was local to it.
- `desktop-package.yml`'s `resolve` works out the main-push auto-minor and the dispatch paths from `github.event_name` and its dispatch inputs. Neither path reads anything only `workflow_call` provides. A `v*` stable cut still raises the auto-minor baseline, because `resolve` reads tags through the API.
- `git grep` finds no remaining doc claim that a server tag attaches installers.

## Not verified

- I could not run the release workflow. Everything above comes from reading it. The first real proof will be the next `v*-rc.N` tag: it should open a prerelease with no desktop assets, and no `desktop-package` run should start.
- `desktop-package.yml` was not dispatched. Its triggers are textually unchanged.

entries.title: fleet: a developer agent's tickets build in parallel — no inherited CPU quota, 24 turns
entries.body:
## Why a developer agent's tickets did not progress in parallel

The owner's instance (outcrop, 2026-11-04) had three tickets on `doug-engineering`. All three showed `turn 1 of 12 — waiting on doug-engineering`, and one omp process was running. I read the live instance (read-only), the rc code, and the Hermes v0.22.4 and v0.21.0 source. Where it serialised:

- **Not Talaria.** Dispatch pushed all three. Each run has its own lease, its own Hermes session (`/api/sessions/<run id>/chat/stream`) and its own Hermes run id. The runs engine spawns one task per run, and there is no per-agent lock or busy gate.
- **Not Hermes.** All three turns were inside Hermes at once. Their tool calls interleaved across the three tickets from 17:49 to 18:05, and the shutdown drain reported `3 api_server run(s)`. v0.22.4 drains a FIFO per session. Its only global gate is `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs`, default 10.
- **The container.** A developer agent's workbench jobs build inside the agent's own container. outcrop's chassis, seeded 2026-09-02 from an older template, still carries `cpus: ${AGENT_CPUS:-2}`, and `docker inspect` shows `NanoCpus=2000000000`. The developer render overrode `mem_limit`/`pids_limit` and kept that quota. Three tickets' cargo builds, tests and omp shared two cores, at a load average of 15 on a 32-core host. TALA-92's cold `cargo build -p talaria-api` hit Hermes' 420 s tool ceiling, was killed, and was relaunched. TALA-83 was still wiring omp. Neither was queued behind TALA-93; both ran in place.
- **The next cap.** Hermes' `max_concurrent_runs` of 10 is below `MAX_LIVE_JOBS_PER_AGENT` (16), and it counts chats and crons too. Past it, Hermes answers a 429, Talaria reads `persona gateway 429`, and the session fails.

## Change

- Render: a developer service replaces the chassis's CPU keys with its own:
  - `cpus: ${AGENT_WB_CPUS:-n}`: n is the host's cores less an eighth, at least 2 (32 → 28). It is a ceiling, so cargo, Go and the JVM size their parallelism to it instead of to every core. `AGENT_WB_CPUS=0` means no limit. A chassis `AGENT_CPUS` no longer reaches a developer agent.
  - `cpu_shares: ${AGENT_WB_CPU_SHARES:-512}`: half the default weight, so builds yield to the app and Postgres.
  - Its config gets `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs = 16 + 8`. A def's larger value, or no cap (0, negative, or either quoted, which is how Hermes `int()`s it), stands.
  - All of these apply on a roll (recreate). The changelog and `docs/WORKBENCH.md` say so, and say how to roll.
- `scripts/skills/oh-my-pi`: run steps that may pass five minutes with `terminal(background=true)` and wait with `process_manage wait` (≤ 300 s). No `nohup`/`&` wrappers and no `execute_code` sleep loops. Each job gets its own `--session-dir`.

I weighed and rejected:
- Backgrounding omp with Talaria polling its JSON. That buys no parallelism, because a synchronous turn blocks only its own session. It would also burn the 12-turn cap and duplicate Hermes' own `process_manage`.
- Talaria driving omp directly. That works against `talaria-works-with-hermes-capabilities`.

Both fixes apply to any repo run in a workbench.

Attribution is not part of this PR; the companion observability PR surfaces it. Every outcrop call is booked as `api:fleet-gateway` with no ticket, for two reasons:
- The engineering container was created 2026-09-22, before per-agent keys, so it still runs on the shared key. The 18:43 restart did not change that: 266 more calls were booked the same way. A roll does.
- It runs Hermes v0.21.0, which logs `unknown config keys ignored: session_affinity_header`. Per-ticket booking needs v0.22+.

## Verified
- `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render -p talaria-fleet-budget` passes: 77 and 13 tests, including the CPU block on outcrop's chassis (`cpus` with no `cpu_shares`) and on a quota/period one, the core default (32 → 28, 4 → 3, 2 → 2), and the run cap for numbers, quoted values, negatives and junk.
- `docker compose config` on the rendered lines gives `cpus: 4` with `AGENT_WB_CPUS=4` and no `cpus` with `AGENT_WB_CPUS=0`. A container created with no override reads `NanoCpus=28000000000` and `CpuShares=512`.
- First version, on a `workobs` worktree stack with outcrop's `cpus: ${AGENT_CPUS:-2}` and a real Hermes v0.22.4 Developer Agent:
  - The agent came up uncapped, with `max_concurrent_runs: 24`.
  - Three tickets dispatched in the same second.
  - Six live tickets ran a stand-in build each turn: 8–11 s uncapped, 46–55 s with `docker update --cpus 2`, and 8–10 s with the cap lifted again.
- `bun run gate` passes.

## Not verified
- A real 11+ concurrent-ticket run hitting Hermes' 429 at the default cap. The cap and its default were read from v0.21.0 and v0.22.4 source, not exercised.
- outcrop itself: its agent needs a roll to pick up this render. The live instance was read-only for this work.
