entries.title: [TALA-90] Bug: Viewing a thread doesn't clear the channel unread badge — sidebar count stays active
entries.body:
Ticket: TALA-90 — Bug: Viewing a thread doesn't clear the channel unread badge — sidebar count stays active after reading the thread replies

Fixes the TALA-90 bug: viewing a thread panel and reading its replies never cleared the channel's unread badge.

Root cause: read state was one per-channel cursor (channel_members.last_read_seq) that only the main feed advanced — the feed query excludes thread replies, and the thread panel posted no read at all, while the unread predicates (list_channels, channel_unread_total, shared_rooms_sql) counted every reply past that cursor.

What changed:
- channel_thread_reads table (thread_root_id, user_id, last_read_seq, monotonic like the channel cursor) appended to MIGRATIONS; schema snapshot regenerated.
- POST /api/channels/{id}/read gains a thread arm {threadRootId, seq?}: advances the per-thread cursor (greatest, never backwards), seq absent means the thread's newest complete reply computed server-side, and when the cursor covers that reply the thread's OWN bell rows clear via new clear_channel_thread_notifications — by group_key (reply:<root>), not the href sweep, which would over-clear @mention rows sharing the channel's href. Whole-channel arm unchanged.
- All three unread-predicate spellings now exclude replies whose thread cursor covers them, so the rail pill, the rail badge and the profile drawer's shared rooms agree.
- ThreadPanel.svelte posts the thread read while the person is looking (same lib/looking rules as the main feed), on open and on live reply arrival, and invalidates the channels query so the sidebar badge drops immediately.

Verification: cargo fmt/clippy (-D warnings, incl. --tests) + unit tests on talaria-channels/notify/routes-comms/api; both new #[ignore]d live tests (unread_predicates_honor_the_thread_cursor, thread_read_clears_only_its_bell_rows) pass 2/2 against a live Postgres on the branch's migrations; svelte-check 0 errors; ui vitest 99 files / 1261 tests green; bun run check clean; docs/api/comms.md regenerated via docs:api.

Reviewer, look hardest at: the unread predicate's NOT EXISTS clause (three spellings that must never drift), the caught-up gate in the route's thread arm (cursor vs thread max complete seq), and the group_key sweep semantics.

## Plan

Bug: reading a thread's replies does not clear the channel unread badge (TALA-90). Approach: (1) locate the unread-badge computation and the read-receipt path across ui and api — expected touchpoints are the chat store / sidebar channel row in ui/src and the read-receipt route in the api crates; (2) add per-thread read state: opening/focusing the thread panel posts a read receipt scoped to the thread that marks its replies read for that user; (3) make the unread computation count replies per-thread via a per-thread lastReadAt instead of top-level timestamps only, so the sidebar badge agrees with the thread panel and the parent-message thread indicator; (4) cover the live path — a reply arriving while the thread panel is open must not badge the channel (or badges only when closed); (5) verify all surfaces reflecting thread activity: sidebar channel badge, Threads list, inline thread indicator ('1 reply — Last reply ...'). Files: ui chat/thread store + sidebar badge components + thread panel, api read-receipt route/unread aggregation (exact paths confirmed after clone by reading code). Tests: vitest unit tests for the unread computation incl. per-thread read state and live-path behavior, svelte-check, bun run gate; UI verified in a real browser against the local stack when feasible.🔧 Opened by **Doug** (`doug-engineering`) via the Talaria workbench (standard effort). Commits on this branch are authored by the agent.


## Review round — made mergeable, logic checked (2026-11-03)

**Why CI was red**
- `migrations`, `live-tests`, `mcp end-to-end`: the schema snapshot was hand-placed. The new table's two foreign keys sat above `channel_teams'`, where pg_dump sorts them after it. That was not an ordering clash with rc: rc had not touched `pg.ts`, and the new table is still the last MIGRATIONS entry. Regenerated with `cd ui && bun run migrations:snapshot`.
- `fmt + clippy + test (api)`: rustfmt alone, in `api/tests/it/channel_thread_reads.rs`. Clippy and the tests had not run.

**What the review found and changed**
- **The three predicate spellings agreed, as three copies.** They are one macro now, `thread_read_covers_sql!`, and the live test asserts the pill, the rail badge and the profile drawer agree at every step.
- **The whole-channel caught-up gate was not changed, and it had to be.** It still read "the channel cursor covers the newest complete message". The main feed never shows replies, so a channel whose newest message is a reply never caught up from the feed, even with that reply read in its panel. The badge read 0 while the bell kept the channel's @mention and DM rows lit. `channel_read_caught_up` now counts a thread-read reply as read, as the badge does. A thread read that leaves the whole channel caught up runs the channel's href sweep. Otherwise it clears only `reply:<root>`, so an @mention elsewhere keeps its row.
- **The thread arm's own gate was right**: cursor ≥ the thread's newest complete reply. It is now `channel_thread_read_caught_up`, spelled through the same clause.
- **The group_key sweep was right.** Mention rows carry no group key, so `reply:<root>` cannot touch them. The test fixture used a made-up `channel-mention` kind; it now uses the real `mention` kind, plus another thread's row and the activity row.
- **ThreadPanel skipped a switched-to thread.** ChannelView swaps `rootId` without remounting the panel, and seqs are channel-wide, so the bare high-water mark never posted a second thread whose newest reply was older. The panel now keys by root through `readCursorToPost`.
- **The rail's Comms badge lagged.** A thread read refreshed only `['channels']`. The rail rides `['unreads']`, so in the app the pill read 0 while the tab said "Comms 2" for up to 30 s. It now refreshes both.

**Verified**: `bun run gate` on the merged tree. CI's migrations job replayed on scratch postgres:16-alpine: fresh, upgrade from main's ledger, the git-hosts mirror, and a re-run applying 0. Four live tests pass against a worktree Postgres and Redis, one of them through the real router. The whole flow was exercised in the running app with two users: pill, rail badge, bell rows and the route's `cleared` answers at each step.

**Seen while exercising, not changed here (pre-existing on rc)**
- **A `['channels']` refetch that changes the open room's row restarts its `/events` stream.** This happens on every message in it. ChannelView reads `channelId` through the prop getter over Comms' `selected` derived, so the effect re-runs, and a fresh stream skips its catch-up. A room event landing in that gap is lost, and the feed's rollups stay stale until the next event.
- **The notification runtime's visit rule reads every direct/following row on the page's href.** So on `/comms/channel/<id>`, an @mention clears on sight within a minute of input, whatever the read route decides.
- **Two DM-only surfaces still count replies past the channel cursor without the thread cursor**: the daily brief's comms lines and inbox focus's channel items.

## Review round 2 — the FIX-FIRST review (2026-11-03)

- **B1, the unread clause ran 5–6× slower.** `thread_read_covers_sql!` is now a bare `exists`, and every caller negates it as a top-level `not exists`, so Postgres plans an anti-join. A new migration adds `channel_thread_reads_user_idx (user_id, thread_root_id) include (last_read_seq)`; the snapshot was regenerated with `migrations:snapshot`.
  - Measured on stock PG16 (50 rooms × 10k messages, 250k thread reads), using the binaries' own SQL, checked byte for byte. Plain execution, 100 unread per room:
    - `channel_unread_total`: PR 379 ms → 211 ms (rc 174 ms). The PR's full JIT, 404 ms of it, is gone.
    - `list_channels`: PR 637 ms → 60 ms (rc 56 ms).
  - The drawer's query already JITs fully on rc, at cost 679k, with no thread clause at all. The fix returns it to rc's level.
  - With nothing ever read (cursor 0), `list_channels` is 1.15 s against rc's 0.41 s and the PR's 1.68 s. Its per-room count becomes a nested-loop anti-join, one index probe per candidate, still with no JIT escalation. Closing that gap would take a grouped count instead of a per-room subquery: a follow-up if never-read rooms matter.
- **S1, a streaming reply left the bell lit.** `notify_channel_post` files no `thread-reply` row for a follower whose thread cursor already covers the reply, so a reply watched while it streamed doesn't light the bell. `ChannelPost` now carries the message id. Covered by a new live test.
- **S2, threads past 299 replies never cleared.** A full thread page (the oldest 300 rows) posts no `seq`, and posts again on each refetch, so the server reads to the newest complete reply.
- **S3, every reply fired its own requests.** Replies landing in a burst are now one POST and one pair of refetches: trailing 750 ms, with a 3 s ceiling. A thread that was just opened reads at once.
- **N4, the reference lost its field notes.** The `// doc:` method note and the two field notes are back in `docs/api/comms.md`, regenerated.
- **N5:** the live-test count above is out of date. `api/tests/it/channel_thread_reads.rs` now has five, all passing.

**Verified**:
- `bun run gate`.
- CI's migrations job replayed with 539 statements.
- The five live tests pass.
- The worktree-stack exercise passes, 19 checks: pill and rail clear on screen, the @mention case, the thread switch, the main feed's read, and a 320-reply thread that clears through a no-`seq` read, plus a 321st reply landing while the panel was open.

The evidence is in the session's `release/tala90/` folder: `06-perf.txt` and `07-exercise-review-round.md`.
